zh_alt: 示意圖：影像上偶然發現一顆腦部病灶時，「常不常見」這個問題有三個不同的分母，以及哪些情況從一開始就不是觀察題。第一段是四個數字、四個分母，每一條都標了族群、年齡與影像條件。Bos 2016 鹿特丹世代研究，5,800 位一般民眾、平均 64.9 歲、做研究用腦部磁振造影，腦膜瘤 2.5%，143 人；同一批人 9.5% 有偶然發現，腦動脈瘤 2.3%，屬非腫瘤性。Morris 2009 的 BMJ 統合分析，16 篇、19,559 位沒有神經症狀的人，各篇影像解析度不同，腫瘤性偶然發現（不分瘤別）0.70%，95% 信賴區間 0.47 到 0.98%；同一份分析裡高解析度序列找到 4.3%、標準解析度只找到 1.7%，機器越好找到的越多。Hall 1994，100 位正常志願者，用專門掃腦下垂體的高解析加對比磁振造影，10% 有 3 到 6 公釐病灶、至少兩位判讀者診斷為腦下垂體腺瘤；這個 10% 不能拿來講一般腦部磁振造影。歐洲神經腫瘤學會 2021 指引自己的講法是一般族群腦部磁振造影 0.9% 到 1.0% 的腦膜瘤，跟上面那條 2.5% 的分母不一樣。圖上註明這四條不可以平均，也不可以挑一條當機率。第三種瘤的分母連單位都換了：一份彙整丹麥、荷蘭、台灣與美國四個族群的系統性回顧指出，散發性前庭神經鞘瘤（聽神經瘤）的發生率是每 10 萬人年 3.0 到 5.2，其中無症狀、偶然診斷的那一小塊，美國 2012 到 2016 年那一筆是每 10 萬人年 1.3；這是每年新診斷的人數，不是掃了有多少人會被找到，放不進同一條軸。那份統合分析的結論句也放在圖上：這些發現在取得腦部磁振造影的知情同意時值得被提及，但不足以支持對健康無症狀的人做篩檢。第二段是「當下沒有動刀，不等於結案」。鹿特丹世代裡因偶然發現被轉給專科醫師的是 188 人、3.2%，其中繼續觀察或第一次門診之後就結案的是 144 人、76.6%。一份 20 篇、2,130 位偶然發現腦膜瘤病人的統合分析顯示，診斷當下的處置分布是主動監測 50.7%、手術 27.3%、立體定位放射手術 22.0%，作者寫在結論裡的是在診斷當下就介入可能導致不必要的過度治療。但主動監測那一格不是空白：同一份統合分析連同 2019 年的勘誤顯示，追蹤期間出現症狀 8.4%，95% 信賴區間 2.8 到 16.7%，最後接受介入 24.8%。另一邊也放上：33 中心、15 國、1,248 人、1,010 顆未治療腦膜瘤的世代裡，383 人、40.5% 在腦膜瘤還沒動靜也沒接受治療的情況下，死於跟腦膜瘤無關的原因。第三段是哪些情況從一開始就不是觀察題，分成三欄，三欄之間畫著「不可合併成一張通用清單」的分隔。腦下垂體腺瘤那一欄來自美國內分泌學會 2011 年偶然瘤指引，列出建議轉介手術的情形：視野缺損；腫瘤壓迫造成的其他視覺異常，例如眼肌麻痺；病灶壓迫造成的神經功能受損；病灶已經貼到視神經或視交叉；合併視覺障礙的垂體中風；泌乳素瘤以外、正在過度分泌荷爾蒙的腫瘤。腦膜瘤那一欄來自歐洲神經腫瘤學會 2021 指引，寫得很短：對大多數有症狀或正在長大的腦膜瘤，第一線治療是手術；同一份指引也寫，第 1 級腦膜瘤仍可能早期復發，第 2 級完全切除的人也可能長期無事，分級與臨床病程之間有相當的個體差異。聽神經瘤那一欄來自美國神經外科醫學會 2018 年聽力保存指引，要反過來理解：已經有單側聽力損失，代表的不是必須馬上治療，而是不能當成沒事；走觀察這條路的人到第十年還維持可用聽力的機率只剩中等偏低，也就是超過 25% 到 50%；所以單側聽力變差的人，第一輪要先正式量一次聽力當基準線。第四段是「良性」和「惡性」在顱內是什麼意思。美國腦瘤登記 2018 到 2022 年的資料裡，非惡性腫瘤的五年相對存活率 91.7%、惡性 34.8%，兩個數字的距離就是良性兩個字的重量。同一個登記 2017 到 2021 年的細項：全體腦膜瘤 195,297 例，其中惡性腦膜瘤 1,608 例；全體腦膜瘤發生率每 10 萬人 10.15，惡性腦膜瘤 0.08。腦下垂體腫瘤的局部侵襲只有每 2,000 顆 1 顆，惡性只有每 10 萬顆 1 顆。圖上註明 91.7% 不是 100%，這個落差也是真的；腦瘤等於腦癌這個等號在這三種病上不成立，但良性也不是結論，只是起點。圖的最後一格是不准的讀法：這張圖不收在「良性所以安心」。圖上沒有一條線通往「所以不用管」，也沒有一條通往「所以要開刀」；要不要治療、什麼時候治療，是醫師依位置、大小、影像特徵與你整體狀況做的判斷。這張圖能替你做的只有一件事：把報告換成可以問出口的問題——我這顆判讀上是哪一種瘤？它有沒有貼到或壓到視神經、視交叉、內耳道、腦幹、靜脈竇？下一次追蹤是幾個月後、照哪一種序列？
en_alt: Schematic on what it means to find something incidentally on a brain scan: the question "how common is this" has three different denominators, and some situations were never a question of observation at all. The first section sets out four numbers and four denominators, each row labelled with its population, its age and its imaging conditions. Bos 2016, the Rotterdam Scan Study, scanned 5,800 people from the general population, mean age 64.9 years, on a research brain MRI: meningioma 2.5%, 143 people; in the same cohort 9.5% had an incidental finding of some kind and 2.3% an intracranial aneurysm, which is not a tumour. Morris 2009, a BMJ meta-analysis of 16 studies and 19,559 people with no neurological symptoms, imaging resolution differing across studies, found neoplastic incidental findings of all tumour types in 0.70%, 95% confidence interval 0.47 to 0.98%; within the same analysis, high-resolution sequences found 4.3% and standard resolution only 1.7%, so the better the scanner, the more it finds. Hall 1994 scanned 100 normal volunteers with a dedicated high-resolution contrast-enhanced pituitary MRI and found lesions of 3 to 6 mm read as a pituitary adenoma by at least two readers in 10%; that 10% cannot be carried over to an ordinary brain MRI. The EANO 2021 guideline uses its own wording, 0.9 to 1.0% of general-population brain MRI scans for meningioma, which is a different denominator from the 2.5% above. The figure states that these four must not be averaged and that none may be picked out as "the" probability. The third tumour changes even the unit: a systematic review pooling Danish, Dutch, Taiwanese and American populations puts the incidence of sporadic vestibular schwannoma, the acoustic neuroma, at 3.0 to 5.2 per 100,000 person-years, of which the asymptomatic, incidentally diagnosed slice was 1.3 per 100,000 person-years in the United States for 2012 to 2016; that is how many people are newly diagnosed each year rather than how many are found when you scan, so it will not go on the same axis. The meta-analysis's own conclusion is quoted: these findings are worth mentioning when consenting for brain MRI, but do not support screening of healthy asymptomatic people. The second section is headed "not operated on today is not the same as closed". In the Rotterdam cohort, 188 people (3.2%) were referred to a specialist because of an incidental finding, and of those 144 (76.6%) were kept under observation or discharged after the first clinic visit. A meta-analysis of 20 studies and 2,130 people with an incidental meningioma shows what was done at diagnosis: active monitoring 50.7%, surgery 27.3%, stereotactic radiosurgery 22.0%; the authors conclude that intervention at diagnosis may lead to unnecessary overtreatment. But the active-monitoring column is not blank: the same meta-analysis, with its 2019 correction, reports that 8.4% developed symptoms during follow-up, 95% confidence interval 2.8 to 16.7%, and that 24.8% went on to have an intervention. The other side is placed alongside it: in a cohort of 1,248 people and 1,010 untreated meningiomas across 33 centres in 15 countries, 383 people (40.5%) died of something unrelated to the meningioma, with the meningioma still quiet and untreated. The third section asks which situations were never a question of observation, in three columns separated by a rule marked "do not merge into one checklist". The pituitary adenoma column comes from the Endocrine Society 2011 pituitary incidentaloma guideline, which lists the situations in which referral for surgery is recommended: a visual field defect; other visual abnormality caused by compression, such as ophthalmoplegia; neurological compromise caused by the lesion pressing on something; a lesion abutting the optic nerves or chiasm; pituitary apoplexy with visual disturbance; and a hypersecreting tumour other than a prolactinoma. The meningioma column comes from the EANO 2021 guideline and is brief: for most symptomatic or growing meningiomas, surgery is the first-line treatment; the same guideline also states that a grade 1 meningioma may still recur early, that someone whose grade 2 meningioma was completely removed may stay well for years, and that there is considerable individual variation between grade and clinical course. The vestibular schwannoma column comes from the CNS 2018 hearing-preservation guideline and has to be read the other way round: unilateral hearing loss already present does not mean treat now, it means this cannot be treated as nothing; for those who take the observation route the chance of still having serviceable hearing at ten years is put at moderately low, greater than 25% to 50%; so anyone with new unilateral hearing loss needs a formal audiogram first, as a baseline. The fourth section explains what benign and malignant mean inside the skull. In the US brain tumour registry for 2018 to 2022, five-year relative survival is 91.7% for non-malignant tumours and 34.8% for malignant ones, and the distance between those two numbers is the weight the word benign carries. In the same registry for 2017 to 2021, of 195,297 meningiomas 1,608 were malignant, with an incidence of 10.15 per 100,000 for meningioma overall and 0.08 for malignant meningioma. Pituitary tumours show local invasion in 1 in 2,000 and are malignant in 1 in 100,000. The figure notes that 91.7% is not 100% and that the gap is real too, that the equation "brain tumour equals brain cancer" does not hold for these three diseases, and that benign is not a conclusion either, only a starting point. The figure closes on the reading that is ruled out: it does not end on "benign, so relax". No line on the figure leads to "so leave it alone" and none leads to "so it must come out"; whether to treat, and when, is a judgement the doctor makes from the site, the size, the imaging features and the patient's health as a whole. The one thing the figure can do is turn a report into questions that can be asked out loud: which of these tumours is mine read as? Is it abutting or pressing on the optic nerve, the chiasm, the internal auditory canal, the brainstem or a venous sinus? When is the next scan, and which sequence?

示意圖：腦膜瘤、前庭神經鞘瘤（聽神經瘤）與腦下垂體腺瘤三種病的分流樹。圖的最上方有一條橫幅寫著：圖上所有發生率與佔比全部來自美國的腦瘤登記，台灣沒有對應數字，原因寫在法律裡。分流樹的起點是「報告上寫著一顆非惡性的顱內腫瘤」，往下分成三條明顯分開的分支，分支之間畫著「預後、門檻、時程不共用」的分隔。第一條是腦膜瘤，第一個問題是分級與位置。它來自腦膜上皮細胞，也就是蛛網膜帽細胞；一篇綜述指出顱底與大腦凸面的腦膜上皮細胞胚胎來源不同，中胚層對神經嵴，這差異影響了各部位好發的組織亞型。第一輪是影像本身——長在哪、貼到什麼、有沒有水腫。歐洲神經腫瘤學會 2021 指引寫，定性診斷通常由神經影像、多半是磁振造影做出，但依世界衛生組織分類定出級別需要手術取得組織，因此無症狀或年長者可以用觀察加追蹤影像的策略來處理。美國登記 2017 到 2021 年的數字是：發生率每 10 萬人 10.15，男 6.02、女 13.90，男女比 0.43，診斷中位年齡 68 歲，195,297 例，其中惡性 1,608 例。第二條是聽神經瘤，第一個問題是聽力。它是前庭神經鞘瘤，解剖上分成內耳道內與延伸到小腦橋腦角兩種，丹麥全國世代就照這個二分法統計。第一輪一定包含一次正式的聽力檢查。整個領域的指引就是繞著聽力寫的：美國神經外科醫學會 2018 年那一份，整份在處理三條路各自的可用聽力保存率，並明訂觀察組在第二年、第五年、第十年的機率級距。美國登記 2017 到 2021 年神經鞘瘤的發生率每 10 萬人 2.02，非惡性 2.01、惡性 0.01，37,436 例；丹麥全國世代的診斷年齡中位數從 1976 年的 49.2 歲升到 2015 年的 60 歲。第三條是垂體瘤，第一個問題是它有沒有在分泌。它來自腺垂體也就是前葉的內分泌細胞；2022 年的世界衛生組織分類把前葉腫瘤跟後葉與下視丘腫瘤分開，以細胞譜系的轉錄因子染色分型。第一輪一定包含抽血看荷爾蒙，貼到視路的話再加視野。美國內分泌學會偶然瘤指引的第一句建議就是分泌問題：完整病史與理學檢查，加上篩檢荷爾蒙過度分泌與腦下垂體功能低下的實驗室檢查；病灶貼到或壓到視神經與視交叉時再加視野。美國登記 2017 到 2021 年垂體腫瘤發生率每 10 萬人 4.67，男 4.03、女 5.41，81,187 例，非惡性佔 99.8% 以上；比利時人口普查式研究裡平均診斷年齡 40.3 歲、女性 67.6%、42.6% 是大腺瘤。圖上並註明垂體這一種明顯比前兩種年輕，所以不要把三種瘤講成「中老年人的病」。接下來一段是兩份登記報告、兩個分母，不可相加。CBTRUS 2018 到 2022 年版：腦膜瘤佔全部原發腦與其他中樞神經系統腫瘤的 42.6%，這個分母含非惡性腫瘤；腦膜瘤佔全部非惡性腫瘤的 57.4%。CBTRUS 2017 到 2021 年版：垂體腫瘤 17.4%、神經鞘瘤 8.0%，報告自己寫這兩者合計略超過全部腫瘤的四分之一，也就是 25.4%。兩格之間畫著「不可相加」的分隔，下方並寫明兩份報告的分母不是同一個，所以三塊不相加。圖上另註：這個登記把非惡性腫瘤與垂體腫瘤都收進來，美國另外幾個癌症登記通常只收惡性腫瘤，報告自己就寫了定義上的差異會影響已發表發生率的直接比較，所以那幾個百分比的分母是腦瘤，不是腦癌。再下一段是台灣沒有這三個數字，而且那不是統計漏掉。癌症防治法第 3 條把癌症定義為「經由病理切片證實，或經其他檢查、檢驗有效推定診斷，在臨床上具有再發或轉移現象之惡性腫瘤」。台灣癌症登記長表摘錄手冊寫申報對象是 ICD-O-3 性態碼為 2、3、6、9 者，同一欄位說明裡 benign（0）與 borderline（1）不在申報範圍，良性腦瘤從一開始就不進癌症登記。113 年度全民健康保險醫療統計年報裡拆得出來的只有 D33，也就是大腦及中樞神經系統其他部位之良性腫瘤：西醫門診 23,027 人、出院 652 件。但 D33 不含腦膜瘤（D32），也不含垂體瘤（D35.2），這兩者在同一份年報裡被歸進「其他腫瘤」那一大類，所以拿 23,027 去代表腦膜瘤或垂體瘤是錯的。三種瘤裡只有聽神經瘤在台灣有一筆可引的發生率，而且是學術研究、不是官方統計：用健保資料庫、以 2001 到 2012 年、20 歲以上、診斷前做過磁振造影者為確定個案，算出年發生率 2.66／10 萬（95% 信賴區間 2.32 到 3.05），60 到 69 歲最高、4.86／10 萬。接著是 PitNET 這個名字的兩邊並陳。改名的那一方是 2022 年世界衛生組織分類，把分化良好的腺垂體腫瘤歸類為腦下垂體神經內分泌腫瘤（PitNETs；過去稱為腦下垂體腺瘤），但實際出版採用的是雙軌命名：腦下垂體腺瘤／腦下垂體神經內分泌腫瘤兩個名字並列。反對的那一方指出，垂體腫瘤的整體盛行率 10% 以上，而局部侵襲只有 1／2,000、惡性只有 1／100,000，用神經內分泌腫瘤這個標籤等於嚴重地錯貼了絕大多數；他們還指出突觸素這類標記也表現在甲狀腺與腎上腺腫瘤上，照同樣的推理那些是不是也要改名。圖上的結語是：它現在有兩個名字，而且沒有定案。最後一段是其他良性顱內腫瘤各有各的邏輯。血管母細胞瘤：一份美國登記分析算出中樞神經系統血管母細胞瘤的發生率 0.141／10 萬人年，多變項分析裡多發腫瘤是較差存活的獨立因子，風險比 1.715，也就是兩組事件發生速度的比值。顱咽管瘤：美國登記 2017 到 2021 年 3,096 例、發生率 0.18／10 萬、佔全部腦瘤 0.7%。表皮樣囊腫：一個 17 例、平均追蹤 126 個月的小腦橋腦角手術系列裡，全切除只有 5 例，其餘 12 例刻意把貼在血管、神經或腦幹上的留下；切除程度與復發風險無關，症狀性復發平均在九年以上之後才出現——切不乾淨也不影響復發，這跟腦膜瘤的邏輯完全相反。圖上註明它們彼此並不相似，不可以讀成「都差不多」。圖的最後一格是不准的讀法：這張圖只做分流，不做預後。三條分支不共用一套預後、一個治療門檻、一張追蹤時程表，把其中一條的數字搬到另一條就是這張圖想擋掉的錯誤。「良性」不是結論，只是起點——這三種瘤都有惡性的那一格，各自的比例不一樣。最實際的一句是：你被排的第一輪檢查長什麼樣子，就看得出醫師把你歸到哪一種；下次門診可以問得很具體——我這一顆算哪一種瘤？依照那一種，第一輪檢查有沒有做齊？
en_alt: Schematic sorting tree for three diseases: meningioma, vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) and pituitary adenoma. A banner across the top states that every incidence figure and every proportion on the figure comes from the United States brain tumour registry, that Taiwan has no corresponding number, and that the reason is written into the law. The tree starts from "the report says a non-malignant intracranial tumour" and divides into three clearly separated branches, with a rule between them marked "prognosis, thresholds and schedules are not shared". The first branch is meningioma, whose first question is grade and site. It arises from the meningothelial cells, the arachnoid cap cells; a review notes that the meningothelial cells of the skull base and of the convexity have different embryonic origins, mesoderm against neural crest, and that this shapes which histological subtypes occur where. The first round is the imaging itself — where it sits, what it abuts, whether there is oedema. The EANO 2021 guideline states that the diagnosis is usually made by neuroimaging, mostly MRI, but that assigning a grade under the World Health Organization classification requires tissue obtained at surgery, so people who are asymptomatic or older can be managed by a strategy of observation and follow-up imaging. From the US registry for 2017 to 2021: incidence 10.15 per 100,000; men 6.02 and women 13.90, a male-to-female ratio of 0.43; median age at diagnosis 68 years; 195,297 cases, of which 1,608 malignant. The second branch is vestibular schwannoma, whose first question is hearing. Anatomically it divides into intracanalicular tumours and tumours extending into the cerebellopontine angle, and the Danish national cohort keeps its statistics on exactly that division. The first round always includes a formal audiogram. The whole guideline literature is built around hearing: the 2018 CNS guideline is given over to the serviceable hearing preservation rate of each of the three routes and sets out the probability bands for the observation group at two, five and ten years. From the US registry for 2017 to 2021, schwannoma incidence is 2.02 per 100,000, non-malignant 2.01 and malignant 0.01, from 37,436 cases; in the Danish national cohort the median age at diagnosis rose from 49.2 years in 1976 to 60 years in 2015. The third branch is pituitary adenoma, whose first question is whether it is secreting. It arises from the endocrine cells of the anterior pituitary; the 2022 World Health Organization classification separates anterior lobe tumours from posterior lobe and hypothalamic tumours and types them by transcription-factor staining for cell lineage. The first round always includes blood tests for hormones, with visual fields added if it touches the visual pathway. The first recommendation in the Endocrine Society incidentaloma guideline is about secretion: a full history and examination plus laboratory screening for hormone hypersecretion and for hypopituitarism, with visual field testing added when the lesion abuts or compresses the optic nerves and chiasm. From the US registry for 2017 to 2021, pituitary tumour incidence is 4.67 per 100,000, men 4.03 and women 5.41, from 81,187 cases, over 99.8% of them non-malignant; in a Belgian cross-sectional study the mean age at diagnosis was 40.3 years, 67.6% were women and 42.6% were macroadenomas. The figure notes that this third one is clearly younger than the other two, so none of the three should be described as a disease of older people. The next section sets out two registry reports, two denominators, which must not be added together. From the CBTRUS 2018–2022 report: meningioma makes up 42.6% of all primary brain and other central nervous system tumours, a denominator that includes non-malignant tumours, and 57.4% of all non-malignant tumours. From the CBTRUS 2017–2021 report: pituitary tumours 17.4% and schwannomas 8.0%, which the report itself describes together as slightly more than a quarter of all tumours, 25.4%. A rule between the two panels is marked "do not add up", and a note below states that the two reports do not share a denominator, so the three shares are not added up. The same note records that this registry includes non-malignant tumours and pituitary tumours while several other American cancer registries usually collect only malignant tumours, that the report itself states that differences in definition affect the direct comparison of published incidence, and that the denominator of those percentages is therefore "brain tumour", not "brain cancer". The following section explains that Taiwan does not have these three numbers and that this is not an oversight. Article 3 of the Cancer Control Act defines cancer as a malignant tumour confirmed by pathological section, or effectively presumptively diagnosed by other examination or testing, which clinically shows recurrence or metastasis. The Taiwan Cancer Registry long-form abstracting manual states that what must be reported is ICD-O-3 behaviour codes 2, 3, 6 and 9, and the same field note places benign (0) and borderline (1) outside the scope of reporting, so benign brain tumours never enter the cancer registry in the first place. In the National Health Insurance medical statistics annual report for ROC year 113 (2024) the only line that can be separated out is D33, benign neoplasm of brain and other parts of the central nervous system: 23,027 people in western-medicine outpatient care and 652 inpatient discharges. But D33 contains neither meningioma (D32) nor pituitary adenoma (D35.2); both are folded into the "other tumours" category in the same report, so using 23,027 to stand for meningioma or pituitary adenoma is wrong. Of the three, only vestibular schwannoma has a citable Taiwanese incidence, and it is an academic study rather than official statistics: using the National Health Insurance database, taking adults over 20 between 2001 and 2012 who had an MRI before diagnosis as confirmed cases, the annual incidence was 2.66 per 100,000 (95% confidence interval 2.32 to 3.05), highest at ages 60 to 69 at 4.86 per 100,000. The figure then sets both sides of the name PitNET side by side. The side that renamed it is the 2022 World Health Organization classification, which classifies well-differentiated adenohypophyseal tumours as pituitary neuroendocrine tumours, PitNETs, previously called pituitary adenomas — but what was actually published uses dual naming, pituitary adenoma / pituitary neuroendocrine tumour, the two names side by side. The side that objects points out that the overall prevalence of pituitary tumours is over 10% while local invasion occurs in only 1 in 2,000 and malignancy in only 1 in 100,000, so that the neuroendocrine tumour label amounts to grossly mislabelling the overwhelming majority; they also point out that markers such as synaptophysin are expressed in thyroid and adrenal tumours too, and ask whether the same reasoning would rename those as well. The figure concludes that it now has two names and that the matter is not settled. The last section notes that other benign intracranial tumours each have their own logic. Haemangioblastoma: an analysis of a US registry puts the incidence of central nervous system haemangioblastoma at 0.141 per 100,000 person-years, and in multivariable analysis multiple tumours were an independent factor for worse survival, hazard ratio 1.715, that is, the ratio of the rate at which events occur in the two groups. Craniopharyngioma: US registry 2017–2021, 3,096 cases, incidence 0.18 per 100,000, 0.7% of all brain tumours. Epidermoid cyst: in a surgical series of 17 cerebellopontine angle epidermoid cysts followed for a mean of 126 months, only 5 were completely removed and in the other 12 the part stuck to a vessel, a nerve or the brainstem was deliberately left behind; the extent of removal was unrelated to the risk of recurrence and symptomatic recurrence appeared on average more than nine years later, which is the exact opposite of the logic for meningioma. The figure notes that these do not resemble one another and must not be read as much the same. The figure closes on the reading that is ruled out: it sorts, and it does not give a prognosis. The three branches do not share a prognosis, a treatment threshold or a follow-up schedule, and carrying a number from one branch across to another is exactly the mistake the figure is built to block. "Benign" is not a conclusion, only a starting point, since each of the three has a malignant box and the proportion in it differs. The most practical line is that what the first round of tests looks like shows which of the three the doctor has sorted the patient into, so the question to ask is specific: which of these is mine counted as, and on that basis, has the first round been done in full?

9.4%；而且顱底腦膜瘤比較常以神經功能缺損表現，非顱底腦膜瘤比較常以癲癇表現。接著是逐個位置的走法，每一條都標明是腦膜瘤而且只有腦膜瘤。前顱窩（嗅溝、眶額、前大腦鐮）：診斷時往往已經很大；視力受損 54%、頭痛 48%、嗅覺喪失 40%、癲癇 20%，可伴人格解構式的行為改變；這些百分比來自診斷時已經很大的族群，不能套到偶然發現的小瘤上。矢狀竇旁：可以長到相當大才有症狀，常以從下肢開始的傑克遜癲癇或頭痛表現，進展期特徵性地出現視乳突水腫與同側偏盲。鞍結節：通常以隱匿的單側視力喪失表現，接著另一眼出現暗點——是一隻眼睛慢慢看不清楚，再換另一隻。外側蝶骨嵴：常以無痛的單側眼球突出表現，接著同側視力喪失。岩斜區：步態失調與顱神經病變，例如三叉神經受損。前床突：各式視覺障礙、顱神經麻痺、眼球突出。後顱窩：可造成阻塞性水腦，表現為視乳突水腫與清晨頭痛。竇匯周圍：枕部局部疼痛、視乳突水腫、同側視野缺損，加上失調與眼球震顫。脊髓：最常在胸椎，表現為緩慢進展的痙攣性輕癱，可伴神經根痛或夜間痛，頸椎與顱頸交界是第二常見。貼近骨頭：局部骨質增生，綜述說這幾乎必然是腦膜瘤細胞侵犯骨頭的徵象，可造成隆起與疼痛。第三段是小腦橋腦角這個位置不是只有聽神經瘤，分成三格：腦膜瘤這一格，小腦橋腦角有 2 到 11% 的腦膜瘤；聽神經瘤這一格，丹麥全國世代把前庭神經鞘瘤分成內耳道內與延伸到小腦橋腦角兩種，自然病程不同、統計也分開做，所以報告上寫小腦橋腦角病灶時那句話還沒把病名講完；表皮樣囊腫這一格，這裡也是它的好發位置，那個 17 例的手術系列收的就是這裡的表皮樣囊腫。第四段是單側聽力變差什麼時候該去照影像，來源是美國神經外科醫學會 2018 年篩檢指引，講的是聽神經瘤：依聽力圖，建議對兩個以上相鄰頻率有 10 dB 以上兩耳差異，或單一頻率有 15 dB 以上差異的人做磁振造影篩檢，以減少沒被診斷出來的聽神經瘤；若要減少照了卻沒診斷出東西的檢查量，可改成只針對 3000 赫茲單一頻率兩耳差異 15 dB 以上的人篩檢。同一份指引也把不好看的那面寫出來了：因為不對稱耳鳴去做磁振造影，診斷出聽神經瘤的比率不到 1%；因為突發性感音神經性聽損去做，不到 3%。這兩個數字同時支持該查跟查到的機會其實不高。台灣端有自己的文字：健保醫療費用審查注意事項編號 100901030 列出耳科病人有下列臨床狀況時，可予以適度安排電腦斷層或磁振造影共十項，包括聽性腦幹反應懷疑耳蝸後病變、單側聽損 2 至 4 千赫損失大於 65 dB、語音辨識分數差、有神經學局部徵象、脈動性耳鳴、不尋常的眩暈或中樞型眼震等；它的門檻跟前面那份指引不是同一把尺，一個講兩耳差幾 dB、一個講單耳掉幾 dB，並陳就好。圖上並標明：這條線是寫給開單的醫師用的，不是給你拿自己的聽力圖對照用的。第五段是垂體瘤往哪個方向長。向上最常見：鞍膈與它的開口對腫瘤擴張是個很弱的屏障，腫瘤可能壓迫並傷害視神經與視交叉；視交叉位置偏後的人，腫瘤會往前長到額葉下方，偏前的人則往後長到第三腦室與下視丘。向下造成蝶鞍重塑、擴大與骨質吸收，為往蝶竇擴散留下通路。向前侵入蝶骨平台、額葉下表面與篩竇。向後擴張到腳間池與腦幹。向側則是擴張進入或侵犯海綿竇。侵襲並不罕見：多達 35% 的腺瘤類型表現出肉眼可見的侵襲，大腺瘤的比例更高。所以美國內分泌學會的偶然瘤指引才會規定，病灶貼到或壓到視神經與視交叉的人要做視野檢查，追蹤期間 6 個月與每年各一次。病人最先報告的是什麼，一份 654 人的瑞典研究分得很清楚：非功能性腺瘤是頭痛與視覺障礙，泌乳素瘤是月經不規則與頭痛，肢端肥大症是外觀改變與打鼾，庫欣氏病是體重增加與疲倦。第六段是位置重要不代表大小可以不管，兩條都標著腦膜瘤：一份 2,130 人的統合分析裡，直徑 3 公分以上是主動監測期間出現症狀的相關因子，但它的 95% 信賴區間寬到只能講方向、不能講倍數；一個 441 人、459 顆偶然發現腦膜瘤的預後模型裡，腫瘤體積增加的風險比是 2.17，95% 信賴區間 1.53 到 3.09，風險比是兩組事件發生速度的比值，大小是模型裡的參數之一，不是能丟掉的東西。反過來也要講：位置再典型，也有人完全沒感覺——那 9.4% 無症狀的腦膜瘤就是這樣被撞見的；同一個位置也可以是不同級別，歐洲神經腫瘤學會明講分級與臨床病程之間有相當的個體差異。圖的最後一格是不准的讀法：這張圖不是給你對號入座的表。上面那些對應都是族群層級的，反過來從症狀推位置、或從位置推自己會怎樣，都會出錯。位置真正決定的是三件事：誰先接手——貼到視路就有眼科與內分泌科的事，長在內耳道就有神經耳科的事；第一輪要多量什麼——視野、聽力、荷爾蒙，該量的那一項不能漏；追蹤要盯哪個方向——往上長跟往側長，看的東西不一樣。下次門診可以把問題問成：我這顆貼到或壓到哪一個構造？因為這個位置，第一輪檢查應該多哪一項？追蹤影像要特別看哪一個方向？
en_alt: Schematic on how the site of a benign brain tumour maps to symptoms, with one hand-drawn anatomical diagram shared by all three tumours. The anatomical drawing is hand-drawn, not to scale and not an anatomical reference; its eleven numbered points are coloured by tumour — gold for meningioma, green for vestibular schwannoma, blue for pituitary adenoma. The numbered points are: 1 convexity (meningioma); 2 parasagittal and falx (meningioma); 3 anterior fossa, including the olfactory groove and orbitofrontal region (meningioma); 4 sphenoid wing and middle fossa (meningioma); 5 tuberculum sellae, against the visual pathway (meningioma); 6 the pituitary gland in the sella (pituitary adenoma); 7 petroclival region (meningioma); 8 internal auditory canal and cerebellopontine angle (vestibular schwannoma); 9 posterior fossa and around the torcula (meningioma); 10 intraventricular (meningioma); 11 spinal cord, which is a separate site code (meningioma). The first section gives the distribution of meningioma by site, as ranges rather than single numbers, from a review pooling several series: convexity 20 to 37%; parasagittal 13 to 22%, of which falx 5%; skull base 43 to 51% in total, broken down into anterior skull base 10 to 20%, sphenoid wing and middle fossa 9 to 36%, and posterior fossa 6 to 15%, of which cerebellopontine angle 2 to 11% and petroclival under 1% to 9%; intraventricular 1 to 5%; orbit under 1% to 2%; spinal cord 7 to 12%. The figure notes that the spinal row needs care, because the US brain tumour registry counts the spinal meninges as a separate site code, so the denominator is not the same. Site is related to grade as well, still for meningioma: the same review states that grade 1 meningiomas are more often at the skull base and higher-grade ones more often at the convexity, parasagittally, on the falx, at the torcula and intraventricularly; a pathological analysis of 2,608 meningiomas points the same way, with the Ki-67 proliferation index of skull base meningiomas significantly lower than that of convexity meningiomas, which holds after stratifying within the same grade. The second section gives what meningiomas present with: headache 33.3 to 36.7%, focal cranial nerve deficit 28.8 to 31.3%, seizure 16.9 to 24.6%, cognitive change 14.4%, weakness 11.1%, no symptoms 9.4%; and skull base meningiomas more often present with a neurological deficit, non-skull-base ones more often with a seizure. It then goes site by site, each line labelled as meningioma and only meningioma. Anterior fossa (olfactory groove, orbitofrontal, anterior falx): often already large at diagnosis, with impaired vision 54%, headache 48%, loss of smell 40% and seizure 20%, sometimes with disinhibited changes in personality; these percentages come from a population already large at diagnosis and cannot be applied to a small incidental tumour. Parasagittal: can grow quite large before causing symptoms, often presenting with a Jacksonian seizure starting in the leg or with headache, and in the advanced stage characteristically papilloedema and a homonymous hemianopia. Tuberculum sellae: usually presents with insidious unilateral visual loss followed by a scotoma in the other eye — one eye gradually dims, then the other. Lateral sphenoid wing: often painless unilateral proptosis followed by ipsilateral visual loss. Petroclival: gait ataxia and cranial neuropathy, for example trigeminal involvement. Anterior clinoid: visual disturbance of various kinds, cranial nerve palsy, proptosis. Posterior fossa: may cause obstructive hydrocephalus, presenting as papilloedema and morning headache. Around the torcula: local occipital pain, papilloedema, an ipsilateral visual field defect, with ataxia and nystagmus. Spinal cord: most often thoracic, presenting as slowly progressive spastic paraparesis, sometimes with radicular or nocturnal pain, with the cervical spine and craniocervical junction second commonest. Against bone: local hyperostosis, which the review says is almost invariably a sign of bone invasion by meningioma cells and which can cause a swelling and pain. The third section states that the cerebellopontine angle is not only vestibular schwannoma, in three boxes. Meningioma: 2 to 11% of meningiomas are in the cerebellopontine angle, the same row as in the table above. Vestibular schwannoma: the Danish national cohort divides it into intracanalicular tumours and tumours extending into the cerebellopontine angle, whose natural history differs and whose statistics are kept separate, so a report saying "cerebellopontine angle lesion" has not yet named the disease. Epidermoid cyst: this is a site where they occur too, and the series of 17 cases was of epidermoid cysts here. The fourth section covers when new unilateral hearing loss should be imaged, from the CNS 2018 screening guideline for vestibular schwannoma: on the audiogram, MRI screening is recommended for people with an interaural difference of 10 dB or more at two or more adjacent frequencies, or of 15 dB or more at a single frequency, to reduce the number of undiagnosed vestibular schwannomas; to reduce the number of scans that diagnose nothing, this can be narrowed to an interaural difference of 15 dB or more at the single frequency of 3000 Hz. The same guideline sets out the unflattering side: MRI done for asymmetrical tinnitus diagnoses a vestibular schwannoma in under 1% of cases and MRI done for sudden sensorineural hearing loss in under 3%, and both numbers support "it should be looked for" and "the chance of finding it is low" at once. Taiwan has its own wording: item 100901030 of the National Health Insurance review guidance lists ten clinical situations in which CT or MRI may reasonably be arranged for an otological patient, including auditory brainstem response suggesting retrocochlear disease, unilateral hearing loss of more than 65 dB at 2 to 4 kHz, poor word recognition scores, focal neurological signs, pulsatile tinnitus and unusual vertigo or central nystagmus; its threshold is not the same ruler as the guideline above, one counting the difference between the ears in dB and the other the loss in one ear, and both are set out without ranking. The figure states that this line is written for the doctor who orders the scan and is not for comparing your own audiogram against. The fifth section covers the direction a pituitary adenoma grows. Upward is commonest: the diaphragma sellae and its opening are a weak barrier to expansion and the tumour may compress and damage the optic nerves and chiasm; where the chiasm sits posteriorly the tumour grows forward under the frontal lobe, and where it sits anteriorly, backward into the third ventricle and hypothalamus. Downward causes remodelling, enlargement and bone resorption of the sella, leaving a route into the sphenoid sinus. Forward means invasion of the planum sphenoidale, the undersurface of the frontal lobe and the ethmoid sinuses. Backward means expansion into the interpeduncular cistern and against the brainstem. Laterally means expansion into or invasion of the cavernous sinus. Invasion is not rare: up to 35% of adenoma types show gross invasion, and the proportion is higher for macroadenomas. This is why the Endocrine Society incidentaloma guideline requires visual field testing for anyone whose lesion abuts or compresses the optic nerves and chiasm, at 6 months and then annually during follow-up. A Swedish study of 654 people is clear about what patients report first: non-functioning adenomas, headache and visual disturbance; prolactinoma, irregular periods and headache; acromegaly, a change in appearance and snoring; Cushing's disease, weight gain and fatigue. The sixth section states that site mattering does not mean size can be ignored, with both lines labelled meningioma: in a meta-analysis of 2,130 people a diameter of 3 cm or more was a factor associated with developing symptoms during active monitoring, but its 95% confidence interval is wide enough that only the direction, not a multiple, can be stated; and in a prognostic model of 441 people and 459 incidental meningiomas the hazard ratio for increasing tumour volume was 2.17, 95% confidence interval 1.53 to 3.09, a hazard ratio being the ratio of the rate at which events occur in the two groups, so size is one of the parameters in the model and not something that can be discarded. The other way round has to be said too: however typical the site, some people feel nothing at all, and that 9.4% of meningiomas with no symptoms is exactly how they are stumbled upon; the same site can also be a different grade, and the EANO guideline states plainly that there is considerable individual variation between grade and clinical course. The figure closes on the reading that is ruled out: this is not a chart for placing yourself on. All the correspondences above are at the level of populations, and reasoning backwards from a symptom to a site, or forwards from a site to what will happen to you, goes wrong. What the site really settles is three things: who takes the case first, since touching the visual pathway brings in ophthalmology and endocrinology while sitting in the internal auditory canal brings in neuro-otology; what else to measure in the first round, since visual fields, hearing and hormones each apply to one of them and the one that applies must not be left out; and which direction to watch on follow-up, since growing upward and growing laterally are watched for different things. At the next clinic visit the questions to ask are: which structure is mine abutting or pressing on, what should be added to the first round of tests because of that site, and which direction should the follow-up scan look at?

顆體積增加；同一份研究還說生長型態有五種，其中 S 型佔 35%，超過六成是自限性的，拿今年的速率推十年後方法上就是錯的；生長速率跟年齡有關，不到 55 歲每年 0.10 立方公分、55 到 75 歲 0.24、超過 75 歲 0.85。右邊是複合惡化終點，IMPACT 外部驗證，JAMA Oncology 2026，33 中心、15 國、1,248 人、1,010 顆未治療腦膜瘤、中位追蹤 61 個月，終點的定義是生長加症狀加腦膜瘤相關死亡加失去可治癒時機，結果十年無惡化 85.7%，五年 88.1%；同一個世代裡 383 人、40.5% 在腦膜瘤沒動靜、也沒接受治療的情況下死於別的原因。圖上寫明：七成五會長大，跟十年有八成五不會惡化，同時是真的，所以正確的句子是「大多數不會因此出事」，而且要講清楚是用哪一把尺量的。另外附一段：一份 20 篇、2,130 人的統合分析連同 2019 年勘誤給的是，主動監測期間出現症狀 8.4%，95% 信賴區間 2.8 到 16.7%，24.8% 最後接受介入，多數惡化的病人都在診斷後五年內發生。第三段是聽神經瘤的觀察，價格是聽力。Kirchmann 2017：156 位內耳道內聽神經瘤、保守處置、平均追蹤 9.5 年，純音平均聽閾從 51 dB 惡化到 72 dB，語音辨識分數從 60% 掉到 34%，AAO-HNS 甲級聽力的人從 19% 掉到 3%，腫瘤生長 37%，保守處置失敗 15%。同一批 156 人、同一次追蹤，換一套評分系統，答案差 24 個百分點：以 AAO-HNS 甲乙級算，可用聽力保存率 34%；以語音辨識分數的一、二級算是 58%。圖上把兩條並排畫成長條，並註明同一批人、同一次追蹤，只是換了評分系統，所以看到任何一個保存率數字，先問一句你用的是哪一把尺。美國神經外科醫學會聽力保存指引把觀察組維持可用聽力的機率列為第 2 年超過 75% 到 100%、第 5 年超過 50% 到 75%、第 10 年超過 25% 到 50%，並指出最一致的預測因子是治療前的聽力與腫瘤沒有生長。聽神經瘤的生長定義是最大徑增加 2 公釐：丹麥全國 1976 到 2015 年的 3,637 例散發性聽神經瘤裡，2,312 人接受觀察、平均追蹤 7.33 年，生長的定義是線性測量增加超過 2 公釐，依東京 2001 共識；依位置分開，診斷後五年曾生長的比例是內耳道內 21%、延伸到小腦橋腦角 37%，十年是 25% 與 42%，生長主要發生在最初五年；因生長轉為積極治療的是 434 人、19%。長了不等於會一直長：一份四中心、592 位已量到生長卻仍繼續觀察的病人研究顯示，從第一次偵測到生長算起，五年內沒有再長的比例是內耳道內 32%、小腦橋腦角 22%；作者的結論是觀察期間偵測到的生長未必預示未來會生長，在適當選擇的病人身上容忍一些生長是站得住的，而那個限定詞不能拿掉，適不適合是醫師選的。第四段是垂體瘤的觀察量的是三件事，尺又換了，用的是每 100 人年的事件率：大腺瘤每 100 人年 12.5（95% 信賴區間 7.9 到 17.2）、實質性病灶 5.7、微腺瘤 3.3、新發生的內分泌功能異常整體 2.4、囊性病灶 0.05。來源是一份 11 篇、追蹤三到十五年的系統性回顧與統合分析；垂體中風與視野缺損惡化都很罕見；作者把這批證據的品質評為非常低，並註明有明顯異質性。垂體瘤的觀察不只照影像，那份指引同時要求視野與內分泌檢查。第五段是什麼讓觀察停下來、什麼讓追蹤鬆開。腦膜瘤是有症狀或正在長大；聽神經瘤是量到生長之後依位置分流，內耳道內多半繼續觀察，延伸到小腦橋腦角的多半開刀；垂體瘤照內分泌學會那張手術清單：視野缺損、壓迫造成的視覺異常或神經受壓、病灶貼到視路、合併視覺障礙的垂體中風、泌乳素瘤以外的過度分泌腫瘤。什麼時候可以鬆開，腦膜瘤這格有研究：一個 441 人的預後模型顯示，追蹤五年之後所有風險組的惡化風險都進入平台；而年齡校正查爾森共病指數 6 分以上的人，例如 80 歲合併慢性腎病，診斷後五年內死於其他原因的可能性是接受介入的 15 倍，不分風險組。但「連續幾年沒變就不用再追」的年數，三份指引都沒寫。圖上並標明：這是醫師用工具分層後的決定，不是你自己可以決定的事；門診裡值得問出口的是，我這一顆，你是用哪一個工具、看哪幾項把我分到這一層的。第六段是台灣端，畫成三道閘門。第一道：適應症有沒有你這一種瘤——支付標準 37028B 與 37029B 的適應症確實寫了「聽神經瘤、腦膜瘤、腦下垂體瘤、顱咽管瘤」。第二道：且須符合下列條件之一——「A.曾接受開顱手術，但有殘餘腫瘤或腫瘤復發者。B.開顱手術可能造成神經損傷或危險性大者。C.有嚴重心肺疾病或其他內科疾病，不適合侵入性手術或全身麻醉者。……F.顱內單側小腦橋腦角聽神經瘤寬度小於 2.5 公分（不含內耳道）者。」第三道：全部個案須事前專案向保險人申請，條文逐字，這一道沒有例外。出口寫的是：條文把放射手術放在「開刀走不通或風險太大」之後，不是第一步，這解釋了為什麼台灣的第一步常是觀察或手術。至於磁振造影追蹤的頻次，針對這三種瘤的條文在全表裡查不到列項——查不到列項不等於沒有給付，怎麼申報問醫務課。圖的最後一格是不准的讀法：這張圖不說「反正都會觀察」。觀察不是什麼都不做，也不是三種瘤共用一套；三條時程刻意不對齊，就是為了擋掉把其中一條搬去用在另一條。生長速率不是保證——上面每一個長大都綁著一種量法，最大徑還是體積、線性還是複合終點，標籤拿掉數字就不能比。離開診間前把四格填滿：下一次影像是幾月、照哪一種序列；要一起量的東西，聽力、視野、荷爾蒙抽血；哪些狀況要提前回來，請醫師講出你這一顆專屬的那幾項；這次的測量值是最大徑幾公釐或體積幾立方公分，用的是哪一種量法。
en_alt: Schematic on the follow-up schedules for three benign brain tumours and on how the method of measurement decides the answer to "has it grown". The first section shows three guidelines as three deliberately unaligned schedules, with a rule between them marked "not aligned; not interchangeable". The meningioma axis comes from the EANO 2021 guideline at the level of a good clinical practice statement, that is, expert consensus, quoted as: "currently, by consensus, for a suspected meningioma or a grade 1 meningioma, annual MRI for five years is recommended; thereafter intervals may be doubled", with years 1 to 5 marked on the axis and "intervals may then be doubled" at its end. The vestibular schwannoma axis comes from the CNS 2018 imaging guideline as a level 3 recommendation, the lowest, quoted as: "MRI should be performed annually for five years; thereafter the interval may be lengthened provided the tumour is stable", with a note that an updated version appeared in 2026 with different wording and different intervals. The pituitary adenoma axis comes from the Endocrine Society 2011 incidentaloma guideline, for incidentalomas that do not meet the surgical criteria, quoted as: "MRI at 6 months for a macroadenoma and at one year for a microadenoma, with intervals lengthened stepwise thereafter if the size is unchanged; visual field testing at 6 months and annually for those whose lesion abuts or compresses the optic nerves and chiasm; endocrine testing at 6 months and annually for a macroadenoma". The figure states the level of evidence plainly: the meningioma line is expert consensus; every relevant recommendation in the vestibular schwannoma guideline set is level 3, and its authors write in their executive summary that "several well-designed questions and subsequent searches did not yield information sufficient to make meaningful and supportable recommendations"; there is no randomised trial behind these intervals, and the doctor adjusts them to the patient. The second section puts two meningioma numbers in the same frame to show that changing the ruler reverses the answer. On the left, measured by volume: Behbahani 2019, a prospective study of 64 people with an incidental meningioma followed for five years, with growth defined as 15% more volume than baseline, found 75% — that is, 48 tumours — increased in volume; the same study reports five growth patterns of which the S-shaped one accounts for 35% and more than six in ten are self-limiting, so projecting this year's rate ten years ahead is wrong as a method, and growth rate varies with age at 0.10 cm³ a year under 55, 0.24 from 55 to 75 and 0.85 over 75. On the right, a composite progression endpoint: the IMPACT external validation in JAMA Oncology 2026, covering 1,248 people and 1,010 untreated meningiomas across 33 centres in 15 countries with median follow-up of 61 months, defines the endpoint as growth, or symptoms, or meningioma-related death, or loss of the window for cure, and reports 85.7% progression-free at ten years and 88.1% at five; in the same cohort 383 people (40.5%) died of something else with the meningioma quiet and untreated. The figure states that three-quarters growing and 85.7% not progressing at ten years are true at the same time, so the correct sentence is "most will not come to harm from it", stated together with which ruler was used. A further note records that a meta-analysis of 20 studies and 2,130 people, with its 2019 correction, found 8.4% developing symptoms during active monitoring (95% confidence interval 2.8 to 16.7%) and 24.8% going on to an intervention, and that most patients who progressed did so within five years of diagnosis. The third section is headed that for vestibular schwannoma, observation is paid for in hearing. Kirchmann 2017 followed 156 intracanalicular vestibular schwannomas managed conservatively for a mean of 9.5 years: the pure tone average worsened from 51 dB to 72 dB, the word recognition score fell from 60% to 34%, the proportion with AAO-HNS class A hearing fell from 19% to 3%, tumour growth occurred in 37% and conservative management failed in 15%. In the same 156 people at the same follow-up, changing the scoring system moves the answer by 24 percentage points: serviceable hearing was preserved in 34% scored by AAO-HNS classes A and B, and in 58% scored by word recognition score classes 1 and 2. The figure draws these two as bars side by side and notes that it is the same people at the same follow-up with only the scoring system changed, so whenever a "preservation rate" appears, the first question is which ruler it used. The CNS hearing-preservation guideline puts the probability of retaining serviceable hearing in the observation group at greater than 75% to 100% at year 2, greater than 50% to 75% at year 5 and greater than 25% to 50% at year 10, and adds that the most consistent predictors are hearing before treatment and the absence of tumour growth. For vestibular schwannoma, growth means 2 mm more in maximum diameter: of 3,637 sporadic vestibular schwannomas in Denmark between 1976 and 2015, 2,312 people were observed for a mean of 7.33 years, with growth defined as an increase in linear measurement of more than 2 mm following the Tokyo 2001 consensus; split by site, 21% of intracanalicular tumours and 37% of those extending into the cerebellopontine angle had grown by five years after diagnosis, and 25% and 42% by ten years, with growth occurring mainly within the first five years, and 434 people (19%) moving to active treatment because of growth. "It has grown" is not "it will keep growing": a four-centre study of 592 people who kept being observed after growth had been measured found that, counting from the first detection of growth, 32% of intracanalicular tumours and 22% of cerebellopontine angle tumours had not grown again within five years, and the authors conclude that growth detected during observation does not necessarily predict future growth and that tolerating some growth is defensible in appropriately selected patients — a qualifier that cannot be dropped, since who is appropriately selected is the doctor's choice. The fourth section states that for pituitary adenoma observation measures three things, and that the ruler changes again to an event rate per 100 person-years: macroadenoma 12.5 per 100 person-years (95% confidence interval 7.9 to 17.2), solid lesions 5.7, microadenoma 3.3, new endocrine dysfunction overall 2.4, and cystic lesions 0.05. The source is a systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 studies with follow-up of three to fifteen years; pituitary apoplexy and worsening visual field defects were both rare; the authors rate the quality of this evidence as very low and record marked heterogeneity. Observation of a pituitary adenoma is not imaging alone — the same guideline requires visual field and endocrine testing as well. The fifth section covers what stops observation and what loosens follow-up. For meningioma: "symptomatic or growing". For vestibular schwannoma: once growth is measured, sorted by site, with intracanalicular tumours mostly kept under observation and those extending into the cerebellopontine angle mostly going to surgery. For pituitary adenoma: the Endocrine Society surgical list — a visual field defect, visual abnormality or neurological compromise from compression, a lesion abutting the visual pathway, pituitary apoplexy with visual disturbance, or a hypersecreting tumour other than a prolactinoma. On loosening, the meningioma column has a study: a prognostic model of 441 people shows that after five years of follow-up the risk of progression plateaus in every risk group, and that people with an age-adjusted Charlson comorbidity index of 6 or more, an 80-year-old with chronic kidney disease for example, are 15 times more likely to die of another cause than to receive an intervention within five years of diagnosis, regardless of risk group. But none of the three guidelines states a number of unchanged years after which follow-up can stop. The figure records that this is a decision the doctor makes after stratifying with a tool and is not the patient's to make, and that the question worth asking in clinic is which tool was used and which items were looked at to put them in that layer. The sixth section covers Taiwan, drawn as three gates. Gate 1, is your tumour in the indications: the indications for items 37028B and 37029B of the payment schedule do list "acoustic neuroma, meningioma, pituitary tumour, craniopharyngioma". Gate 2, and one of the following conditions must be met: "A. has had a craniotomy but has residual or recurrent tumour. B. craniotomy would risk neurological injury or carries high risk. C. has severe cardiopulmonary or other medical disease making invasive surgery or general anaesthesia unsuitable. … F. a unilateral intracranial cerebellopontine angle acoustic neuroma less than 2.5 cm in width (excluding the internal auditory canal)." Gate 3, every case requires prior case-by-case application to the insurer, word for word from the regulation, with no exception. The exit reads: in plain words, the regulation places radiosurgery after "surgery is not an option or is too risky", not first, which is why the first step in Taiwan is so often observation or surgery. As for how often follow-up MRI is covered, there is no line item for these three tumours anywhere in the schedule — and no line item is not the same as not covered; how to code and claim it is a question for the hospital's medical affairs office. The figure closes on the reading that is ruled out: it does not say "everyone gets observed anyway". Observation is not doing nothing and it is not one prescription shared by three diseases, and the three schedules are deliberately not aligned precisely to block carrying one of them across to another. A growth rate is not a guarantee: every "growth" above is tied to one way of measuring — maximum diameter or volume, a linear measurement or a composite endpoint — and with the label stripped off the numbers cannot be compared. Before leaving the clinic, fill in four boxes: the month of the next scan and which sequence; what is to be measured alongside it, that is hearing, visual fields and hormone blood tests; which situations mean coming back early, asked of the doctor for that tumour specifically; and today's measurement — how many millimetres in maximum diameter or how many cubic centimetres in volume, and by which method.

en_alt: Schematic: how a meningioma is graded, and how two molecular markers bypass the histology to set the grade. Across the top is a scale with only three steps - WHO grade 1, WHO grade 2 and WHO grade 3 as three coloured blocks side by side - with a fourth slot drawn as an empty hatched box marked with a cross and labelled "There is no WHO grade 4 meningioma". The note beside it reads: in the 2021 grading table the meningioma row reads "1, 2, 3", so a report that says grade 3 is at the top of this scale, not third out of four; the scale measures how likely the tumour is to come back and how closely the next few years have to be watched, not life expectancy. The middle of the figure holds three route cards headed "Three routes through the 2021 criteria: whichever is reached first sets the grade". Route A is histopathological features, grade no longer being set by which subtype the tumour resembles: 4 to 19 mitoses per 10 high-power fields gives WHO grade 2; more than 20 gives WHO grade 3; three of the five "soft" atypical criteria gives WHO grade 2. The five are sheeting, hypercellularity, small-cell change, prominent nucleoli and spontaneous necrosis. A note adds that subtype names still appear on the report but no longer set the grade on their own; the source is the International Consortium on Meningiomas 2024 consensus review, labelled meningioma, WHO grades 1 to 3. Route B is brain invasion, one feature alone being enough for WHO grade 2, with a red status pill reading "What it means is not settled": brain invasion on its own is now enough for WHO grade 2, but the same sentence goes on to say that in the absence of other high-grade features the relationship between brain invasion and prognosis remains unclear; and to see brain invasion the specimen has to contain brain tissue, sampling practice differs between countries, and many specimens have nothing to look at. The card closes with a question worth asking out loud: apart from brain invasion, does my report show any other WHO grade 2 feature. Route C is the two molecular markers that set WHO grade 3 without reference to the histology - a TERT promoter hotspot mutation, or a CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion - either one alone being enough; the EANO 2021 guideline says the same thing regardless of whether anaplastic features are present. The same card carries a branch drawn as a dashed line reading CDKN2A/B heterozygous deletion and tagged "Not a grading criterion": the hazard ratio of 5.5, 95 per cent confidence interval 4.0 to 7.6, is not small, but it is not a grading criterion, and a report that says heterozygous does not mean WHO grade 3. Beneath it is the limit ICOM adds: these molecular changes are uncommon in meningioma to begin with and rarer still where the histology looks unremarkable. Below the route cards is a set of horizontal bars headed CDKN2A/B status and median progression-free survival, from an individual patient data meta-analysis of 4 studies and 2,521 patients with a homozygous deletion prevalence of 4.9 per cent: wild type 180.0 months; heterozygous deletion 26.1 months, drawn as a dashed outline and tagged "Not a grading criterion"; homozygous deletion 11.0 months, tagged "to WHO grade 3". Next comes how the three grades divide up, as a single full-width stacked bar - WHO grade 1 80.1 per cent, WHO grade 2 18.3 per cent, WHO grade 3 1.5 per cent - marked as United States registry data graded under the 2021 classification, with a note that the proportions are quoted through the consensus, which does not state the registry report year or the number of tumours. Alongside sits a panel for the 2018 to 2022 CBTRUS report: meningioma is 42.6 per cent of all primary brain and other central nervous system tumours and 57.4 per cent of all non-malignant tumours, and percentages from different report years must never be added to or subtracted from one another; a further line gives ten-year relative survival for non-malignant meningioma as 83.4 per cent. The next panel is the trap in the registry field marked "malignant", tagged "A coding field, not a pathological grade": in the United States SEER series carrying that label only 63.6 per cent were WHO grade 3, with 20.4 per cent WHO grade 1 and 15 per cent WHO grade 2, because the label follows the ICD code rather than central pathology review; the first step on seeing the word is to establish whether it came from the pathology report or from a registry code, since the two can coexist and can disagree. The last card is methylation classification, tagged "A research tool, not a decision tool", in two columns: on the left, "The signal is real" - a 2017 retrospective analysis of 497 meningiomas from 10 European centres sorted methylation profiles into six clinically relevant classes and predicted recurrence better than WHO grading, Brier score comparison p=0.0096, with validation in an independent cohort of 140; on the right, "But it is not yet a decision tool" - the consensus states that a unified molecular classification has still not been established, that sequencing or a methylation array is needed and not every centre has the technology, and that differences in reimbursement and interpretive experience and the unsettled choice of assay all stand in the way; the analysis run on prospective trial specimens, 38 WHO grade 2 and 3 meningiomas from EORTC 22042-26042, pointed the right way but did not reach statistical significance. So to the question whether methylation can decide whether radiotherapy is needed, today's answer is no. At the foot of the figure a gold-bordered panel reads: a grade is the reading of one specimen, not an identity card. The same meningioma can be given a different grade at a different time or a different operation; two pathology reports from different dates with different grades are not two contradictory answers but two points in time. Before any of the later questions can be discussed, four lines on the report are worth circling: the WHO grade, the mitotic count per 10 high-power fields, whether brain invasion is mentioned, and whether TERT or CDKN2A/B were tested. The figure decides nothing; it only shows which four questions to ask.

en_alt: Schematic: where the clinical line between single-fraction and fractionated stereotactic treatment actually comes from, and what level of evidence sits on each side. No platform and no brand name appears anywhere; the only machine-flavoured wording is inside the verbatim Taiwanese insurance item names. The first panel is headed "What actually draws the line is how much the optic nerves and chiasm can take" and is drawn as a dose-fraction bar chart: the maximum point dose to the optic apparatus corresponding to a risk of radiation-induced optic neuropathy below 1 per cent, in people not previously irradiated, is 12 Gy in 1 fraction, 20 Gy in 3 and 25 Gy in 5, with a conventional-fractionation bar at 60 Gy at about 1.8 Gy per fraction. A note states that the conventional bar carries the opposite sense - QUANTEC says toxicity rises clearly above a total of 60 Gy and clearly above 12 Gy in a single fraction - that the authors of the pooled analysis suggest keeping a single fraction to 10 Gy, and that for people irradiated before the risk is roughly ten times higher. The panel also states what QUANTEC calls strong evidence: as the dose per fraction comes down, the total dose the optic pathway tolerates goes up; and it carries the population label for the pooled analysis - 34 studies, 1,578 patients, including cavernous sinus meningioma, pituitary adenoma, craniopharyngioma and malignant skull base tumours, not meningioma alone. In plain words: when the tumour is against the optic nerve or chiasm, the treatment is fractionated. The second panel is the guideline card. On the left are three statements from the EANO 2021 guideline: in well-selected cases with a tumour that is not large, stereotactic radiosurgery is established as an alternative to surgery; for intracranial meningioma under 3 cm in diameter, local control after radiosurgery is comparable to Simpson grade I resection; and for larger tumours the guideline mentions fractionated stereotactic treatment in 2 to 5 fractions. On the right is what the guideline does not say: there is no hard threshold of the form "within so many millimetres of the optic nerve it must be fractionated", and "over 3 cm must be fractionated" is a line drawn by clinical habit. The third panel is two equal-height cards side by side, headed "The two sides did not treat the same size of tumour". The left card is stereotactic radiosurgery, tagged as a retrospective cohort from 15 centres: 4,565 patients and 5,300 benign meningiomas, all treated at least five years earlier, 3,768 tumours analysed after excluding imaging follow-up under 24 months, median imaging follow-up 63 months, median tumour volume 4.8 cm3 and median margin dose 14 Gy. It is labelled "Assessed by: change in volume on imaging", with a stacked bar showing 58 per cent shrank, 34.5 per cent unchanged and 7.5 per cent enlarged, and a list of figures: control rate 92.5 per cent, 5-year progression-free survival 95.2 per cent, 10-year progression-free survival 88.6 per cent, re-treatment needed in 2.2 per cent and permanent complications 6.6 per cent. Beneath it are the two things from the same dataset that have to be said together: control was better at the skull base than at the convexity (p<.001), and control was significantly higher in tumours diagnosed on imaging alone than in pathologically confirmed WHO grade 1 disease (p<.001), which is direct evidence of selection bias. The right card is fractionated stereotactic radiotherapy, tagged as a single-centre retrospective cohort: 317 patients, WHO grade 1 48.3 per cent, WHO grade 2 8.2 per cent and grade unknown 43.5 per cent, median follow-up 5.7 years, median target volume 33.6 cm3 - seven times that of the single-fraction series - and median total dose 57.6 Gy at 1.8 Gy per fraction. A stacked bar shows 70.4 per cent remained stable and 6.9 per cent progressed on imaging at a median of 4.5 years, and the figures are overall local control 93.1 per cent, recurrence 15.5 per cent above 60 cm3 against 4.3 per cent at 60 cm3 or less, pre-existing neurological deficit improved in 42.9 per cent and pre-existing symptoms worsened in 8.2 per cent, with WHO grade 2 tumours failing locally significantly more often (p<0.002) and eight patients developing new symptoms - reduced vision, trigeminal neuralgia, intermittent tinnitus. Between the cards a warning reads: the two sets of numbers must not be set against one another, the volumes differ several times over, a median of 4.8 cm3 against 33.6 cm3. Two smaller panels follow: perioptic meningioma treated with conventional fractionation, transcribed through a review, with pooled local control 99.8 per cent, vision maintained or improved in about 90 per cent, estimated radiation-induced dry eye 10.1 per cent and retinopathy 7.2 per cent; and the time window, in which the commonest problem after single-fraction treatment is radiation-induced brain oedema, with 13 of 26 reviewed studies reporting non-skull-base disease separately, symptomatic oedema 5 to 43 per cent, any oedema 28 to 50 per cent and a mean time to onset of three to nine months after treatment. The fourth panel is the proton therapy card, carrying a red pill reading "This must not be read as proton being better than photon": a meta-analysis of four techniques in WHO grade 1 meningioma only, 24 studies and 4,673 patients, gives 5-year local control of 95.9 per cent for conventionally fractionated proton therapy, 93.0 per cent for conventionally fractionated photon therapy and 95.3 and 89.8 per cent for two stereotactic radiosurgery groups - while the meta-regression showed that neither treatment modality nor tumour volume was significantly associated with local control. Alongside is a proton-only meta-analysis of 19 studies and 1,431 patients (WHO grade 1 70.6 per cent, grade 2 25.2 per cent, grade 3 4.2 per cent) with a pooled complication rate of 16 per cent, 5-year overall survival 91 per cent and mean local control on imaging 71 per cent, all with high heterogeneity. The same card holds a box tagged "Ongoing, primary completion February 2032": COG-PROTON-01 randomises benign cavernous sinus meningioma 1:1 to fractionated proton or photon radiotherapy, 160 patients planned, with cognitive and functional deterioration five years after radiotherapy - not tumour control - as the primary endpoint, recruitment having opened in February 2024. The card closes: the sentence "proton therapy is better for meningioma" has no clinical data behind it today. The fifth panel is the Taiwanese statute card, tagged National Health Insurance fee schedule, effective 1 April 2026: item 37028B, "three-dimensional X-ray knife stereotactic radiosurgery" in the statute's own wording, 82,000 points, for a diameter under three centimetres or a volume of fifteen cubic centimetres or less and three lesions or fewer; and item 37029B, "image-guided intensity-modulated X-ray knife stereotactic radiosurgery", 153,229 points, for a three-dimensional diameter not exceeding 3.5 by 3.5 by 3.5 centimetres or a volume of twenty cubic centimetres and three lesions or fewer. The indications name acoustic neuroma, meningioma, pituitary tumour and craniopharyngioma verbatim, but one of six conditions A to F must also be met: A, has undergone craniotomy but has residual or recurrent tumour; B, craniotomy would carry a risk of neurological injury or substantial danger; C, has severe cardiopulmonary or other medical disease making invasive surgery or general anaesthesia unsuitable; D and E, see the statute; F, unilateral intracranial cerebellopontine angle acoustic neuroma under 2.5 centimetres in width, excluding the internal auditory canal. The statute also requires every case to be submitted to the insurer for prior approval. The last box in this panel reads "The current version has no separate item for fractionated stereotactic treatment", so the insurance codes cannot be used to infer how single-fraction and fractionated treatment are distinguished. At the foot of the figure a gold-bordered panel reads: the question is not which one is better. Ask two numbers about the tumour - its volume, and how far it sits from the optic nerves and chiasm; then two numbers about the plan - if it is a single fraction, where the maximum point dose to the optic apparatus will fall, and if it is fractionated, how many fractions and why that number; and leave the last question for time: during the three to nine months after treatment, how oedema should be watched for and what would mean coming back at once.

級別，還有術後那一次基準磁振造影；要問的第一件事是我到底算全切除還是次全切除，依據是術中判定還是術後影像；接著問兩個相反方向的問題：如果現在不照，多久掃一次、看到什麼會改變決定；如果現在照，劑量與範圍怎麼定，我這個位置最可能傷到的是什麼。這張圖不替任何人做決定，四格之間也不可以直接比較。
en_alt: Schematic: whether radiotherapy should be added after surgery for WHO grade 2 meningioma, shown as four studies side by side in four different states. The first box is ROAM/EORTC-1308, with a gold status pill reading "Closed to recruitment, awaiting results": a randomised phase 3 trial allocating 1:1 to 60 Gy in 30 fractions or active monitoring, eligibility being newly diagnosed solitary WHO grade 2 meningioma with a Simpson 1 to 3 resection and the ability to start radiotherapy within twelve weeks of surgery; recruitment ran from 28 April 2016 to 26 May 2021 and is closed, the target was 190 and 157 were actually recruited, and the overall trial end date is 31 March 2026. Its results field is drawn as a grey box reading "Results not yet published", noting that the registry publications field still holds only the 2015 protocol and a 2020 qualitative analysis. The second box is NRG-BN003, with a blue status pill reading "Still recruiting": a randomised phase 3 trial of radiotherapy against observation, eligibility being WHO grade 2 meningioma after gross total resection, an estimated 163 patients, still open, primary completion 15 June 2027 and overall completion 2032; its results field is likewise a grey box reading "No results yet", noting that an ongoing trial must not be read as a known result. The eligibility criteria of these two boxes are picked out in two differently tinted panels headed "they did not recruit the same people": ROAM takes Simpson 1 to 3, the surgeon's intraoperative judgement, which covers coagulation of the dura and leaving involved dura behind; NRG-BN003 takes patients after gross total resection. Beside them a panel explains why a question asked for ten years is still waiting, tagged "Preprint, not peer reviewed": ROAM's own radiotherapy quality assurance analysis reports that of 56 centres completing the benchmark case 13, or 23 per cent, had major deviations, and that during the trial 28 centres treated 64 patients in all, a median of 2 per centre, with 25 (39 per cent) having to resubmit outlines or plans. The third box is RTOG 0539, its status pill reading "Phase 2, risk-stratified, not randomised", with a ten-year analysis published in 2026. Ten-year progression-free survival for the three groups is drawn as horizontal bars: low risk, n=60 (WHO grade 1, observation after surgery, median follow-up 12.1 years), 85.2 per cent, with 10-year overall survival 94.1 per cent; intermediate risk, n=52 (recurrent WHO grade 1, or newly diagnosed WHO grade 2 after gross total resection, 54 Gy, median follow-up 12.0 years), 72.2 per cent, with 10-year overall survival 84.7 per cent and grade 3 or higher treatment-related toxicity in 5 patients (9.6 per cent); high risk, n=53 (newly diagnosed WHO grade 2 after subtotal resection, newly diagnosed WHO grade 3, or recurrent WHO grade 2 or 3, 60 Gy, median follow-up 11.1 years), 42.5 per cent, with 10-year overall survival 51.1 per cent and grade 3 or higher toxicity in 8 patients (15.1 per cent). A note states that the three group names are in fact the grid produced by crossing grade with whether the tumour was completely removed: the same WHO grade 2 tumour sits in the intermediate group after gross total resection and in the high-risk group after subtotal resection. Two further lines add that the first report of the intermediate-risk group gave a 3-year progression-free survival of 93.8 per cent (p=0.0003) against a historical control of about 70 per cent for gross total resection alone, not a concurrently randomised comparison group; and that EORTC 22042-26042 is a single-arm phase 2 study of 56 patients with WHO grade 2 disease, Simpson 1 to 3, treated to 60 Gy, median follow-up 5.1 years, estimated 3-year progression-free survival 88.7 per cent and grade 3 or higher late signs and symptoms 14.3 per cent. The section closes with a warning: these numbers look good, but not one of them is a randomised comparison of treating against not treating. The fourth box is the observational pooled data, with a grey status pill reading "Observational, not randomised", drawing on 1,452 patients with WHO grade 2 meningioma from 1989 to 2019, of whom 276 (19.0 per cent) had adjuvant fractionated radiotherapy. The observational section opens with interval plots on a log scale with a dashed line at 1: local recurrence after gross total resection, odds ratio 0.50 (0.36 to 0.68), p<0.0001, from 30 studies and 2,904 patients after gross total resection, 737 irradiated and 2,167 not; progression-free survival, hazard ratio 0.849 (0.730 to 0.988), p=0.035, from 23 studies and 3,822 patients; and overall survival, hazard ratio 0.79 (0.57 to 1.11), p=0.173, favouring radiotherapy but not significant. The conclusion drawn is that what the observational data will carry is "recurrence comes later", not "you live longer". Next comes the panel headed "The larger of the two finds no benefit after gross total resection": unadjusted 5-year recurrence after gross total resection was 25.5 per cent among those irradiated and 22.8 per cent among those not, and after G-computation adjustment for age, sex, Simpson grade, Ki-67, location, national health system and year of treatment, the authors write that there is no evidence that adjuvant fractionated radiotherapy lowered the risk of recurrence. This is drawn as an interval plot with the zero line picked out clearly: the largest difference is -2.7 per cent with a 95 per cent confidence interval of -5.6 to 0.2, the zero line marked as meaning no difference, and the note that the interval does not rule out a small benefit but neither does it show that one exists. The same panel carries the finding the authors themselves flag as unexpected - mortality was higher among those irradiated after gross total resection, driven mainly by older patients with a low Ki-67 who nevertheless received radiotherapy - and the paper that points even further the other way: a single centre series of 318 patients with WHO grade 2 disease (1990 to 2023, 104 irradiated, median follow-up 5.1 years) in which adjuvant radiotherapy was associated with markedly worse progression-free survival (p<0.0001 after both gross total and subtotal resection) and worse disease-specific survival after gross total resection (p=0.0237), retrospective single-centre data almost certainly affected by indication bias. A further panel states that subtotal resection is a different box: in the same 1,452-patient analysis the subtotal resection group points more consistently, radiotherapy being associated with a lower risk of recurrence both before and after adjustment, while the low-risk group of RTOG 0539 gives the mirror image, with 10-year progression-free survival of 87.6 per cent after gross total resection and 72.7 per cent after subtotal resection. At the foot of the figure a gold-bordered panel sets out what can be asked for in the years before there is an answer: three things have to be on the table first - the pathology report, the Simpson grade in the operation note, and the baseline postoperative magnetic resonance scan; the first question is whether this counts as gross total or subtotal resection and whether that is based on the intraoperative judgement or the postoperative imaging; then two questions pointing in opposite directions, namely how often the scan would be repeated and what would change the decision if there is no radiotherapy now, and how the dose and field are set and what is most likely to be damaged in this location if there is. The figure decides nothing for anyone, and the four boxes must not be compared with one another.

en_alt: Schematic: progestins and meningioma, with absolute risk and relative risk held in one frame. The top of the figure settles the biggest misunderstanding first: combined oral contraceptives show no association, tagged "Observational meta-analysis, no significant association", the headline figure being a relative risk of 0.93 with a 95 per cent confidence interval of 0.83 to 1.03, from a meta-analysis of 12 case-control and 6 cohort studies; so "taking the pill gives you a meningioma" does not stand up in the evidence. Beside it, pointing the other way, is menopausal hormone therapy: in the same meta-analysis a relative risk of 1.19 (1.01 to 1.40), and 1.32 (1.07 to 1.64) in postmenopausal women; and in a separate meta-analysis of menopausal hormone therapy alone - 11 studies, 1,820,954 people, 3,249 meningiomas - a pooled odds ratio of 1.29 (1.03 to 1.60), with 1.27 in current users, significant, and 1.12 in past users, not significant, the authors writing that whether the association is causal is for later research to establish. The second section is headed "For the ingredients that do carry a signal, this is what the absolute risk looks like", tagged "Per 100,000 person-years, French national health insurance cohorts", and states the outcome definition first: in all of these studies the outcome is surgery or radiotherapy for an intracranial meningioma, not being diagnosed with a meningioma. Each of three ingredients is drawn as a pair of horizontal bars, exposed above and not exposed below, on one shared per-100,000 person-years scale. Cyproterone acetate at high dose, a cohort study in France of more than 250,000 girls and women aged 7 to 70, exposure defined as a cumulative 3 g or more in the first six months: 23.8 cases among the exposed against 4.5 among the unexposed, adjusted 6.6 times (4.0 to 11.1), and above a cumulative 60 g the multiple rises to 21.7 (10.8 to 43.5). Nomegestrol acetate, a French cohort of more than 1.06 million women: 19.3 against 7.0, age-adjusted 2.9 times (2.4 to 3.7), and above a cumulative 6 g the multiple rises to 12.0 (9.9 to 16.0). Chlormadinone acetate, a French cohort of more than 820,000 people: 18.5 against 6.8, 3.1 times (2.4 to 4.0), and above a cumulative 8.64 g the rate approaches 47 per 100,000 person-years. Every multiple sits against its own absolute risk; none appears on its own. The section closes with a passage noting that at the highest point, 23.8 per 100,000 person-years works out at roughly 2.4 in 10,000 for one person in one year; that the European Medicines Agency puts it the same way, calling the side effect rare and affecting roughly 1 to 10 people in every 10,000 depending on dose and duration, with risk rising with cumulative dose; and that the multiple is alarming while the baseline is low, so both have to be held in mind at once. The third section is three columns - signal present, no signal, insufficient data - from a French national case-control study of 18,061 people who had surgery for an intracranial meningioma between 2009 and 2018, matched 1:5 by year of birth and place of residence to 90,305 controls. Signal present: medrogestone, odds ratio 3.49 (2.38 to 5.10); injectable medroxyprogesterone acetate 5.55 (2.27 to 13.56); promegestone 2.39 (1.85 to 3.09), with these excess risks driven by use of more than one year; and the three already known to carry risk read, in the same dataset, cyproterone 19.21 (16.61 to 22.22), nomegestrol 4.93 and chlormadinone 3.87. No signal: progesterone, dydrogesterone and the levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system. Insufficient data: dienogest and hydroxyprogesterone, too few users to draw a conclusion. Beneath the columns the 2026 meta-analysis pulls the picture together: cyproterone acetate, pooled odds ratio 12.36 (7.47 to 20.45), moderate certainty; depot injectable medroxyprogesterone acetate 2.68 (1.72 to 4.19), low certainty; and the authors' own assessment that observational design, residual confounding, heterogeneity and imprecision in some exposures all limit the strength of the evidence. The fourth section gives the population-level figures after stopping, explicitly labelled as data and not as an instruction: for nomegestrol, one year or more after stopping, risk was the same as in the unexposed group, 1.0 (0.8 to 1.3); for cyproterone, one year after stopping, risk was still 1.8 times that of the unexposed group (1.0 to 3.2), clearly down but not all the way back to baseline. The fifth section is Taiwan: of the three ingredients only one is still available. From a record-by-record search of all 72,043 entries in the TFDA full medicinal product licence dataset - cyproterone acetate has several currently valid licences; nomegestrol acetate has one record in the whole dataset, revoked, valid until 15 January 2020; chlormadinone acetate likewise one record, revoked; medrogestone and promegestone have no current records; and all current medroxyprogesterone acetate licences are oral formulations, the injectable formulation having been revoked with validity ending 9 May 2020. The same panel carries TFDA announcement Wei-Shou-Shi No. 1111407692 of 15 September 2022, which under Article 48 of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act requires the Chinese-language package insert of high-dose 50 mg cyproterone-containing products to add to the contraindications section, quoted verbatim, "patients who currently have, or have a history of, meningioma"; to add meningioma-related safety information to the "Warnings and Precautions" and "Pharmacological Properties" sections; to change the indication to "for use only where there is no other treatment option, or where other treatments have been ineffective"; and to add to the dosage section that once clinical symptoms have improved, the lowest effective dose should be used to maintain the effect - the low-dose 2 mg products carrying the same additions. At the foot of the figure is a panel headed "Who to take this question back to". It begins with what not to do: do not stop the medicine on your own, since whether to stop or change it is a decision for the doctor who prescribed it and has to be weighed together with why it was prescribed in the first place. Then four things to ask: take the medicine packet back to the department that prescribed it and establish which ingredient it actually is, reading the English ingredient name rather than the brand name; ask how long it was taken and roughly what the cumulative dose comes to; ask whether a brain magnetic resonance scan is warranted given the current situation; and if stopping is decided on, whether to repeat the scan three months later to see the trend. The last line is for people who already have a meningioma: the association between these medicines and meningioma comes entirely from observational data, and the outcome measured is a meningioma severe enough to need surgery or radiotherapy, so what it tells you is that the question is worth taking to a doctor, not that the medicine caused your tumour.

位內耳道內聽神經瘤、純觀察、追蹤九年半，用 AAO-HNS 的 A 到 B 級算，可服務聽力保存率是 34%；用語音辨識分級的第 1 到 2 級算，同一批人是 58%。兩根長條中間標著「換一把尺＝24 個百分點」，兩根各自附四項標籤：評分系統、追蹤年數九年半、人數 156、治療方式純觀察。第二格是三條路放在同一份文件裡的機率帶，來自美國神經外科醫學會 2018 年的聽力保存指引，三條路共用一套可服務聽力定義（AAO-HNS 的 A 或 B 級，或 Gardner-Robertson 第 1 到 2 級）與同一組時間點：放射手術 2 年 50% 到 75%、5 年 50% 到 75%、10 年 25% 到 50%；顯微手術（小至中型偶發腫瘤）三格都是 25% 到 50%；保守觀察 2 年 75% 到 100%、5 年 50% 到 75%、10 年 25% 到 50%。這一格另標明：基線 A 級者觀察十年那一格，指引寫的是「資料不足，無法判定」；指引沒有給合併人數，因為這是從系統性回顧彙整的級距，不是單一研究；這幾條建議全部是 Level 3 證據，原文動詞是「應該被告知有……的機率」，是說明用的機率帶，不是排名；三條路共通的預後因子只有一組：治療前語音辨識與純音閾值愈好、腫瘤愈小，保存機率愈高。第三格畫 V-REX
