en_alt: Schematic comparing the three management roads for vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma), built around the rule that every hearing-preservation figure must carry four labels: grading system, years of follow-up, number of patients and treatment. It opens with the state of the evidence: there is one randomised trial here, comparing radiosurgery with observation, with tumour shrinkage as its primary endpoint, while surgery versus radiosurgery still rests on retrospective cohorts and meta-analyses alone. The first panel is the pillar of the figure, headed "the same ears, the same audiogram, a different grading system": in 156 Danish patients with an intracanalicular vestibular schwannoma followed for nine and a half years on observation alone, serviceable hearing preservation is 34% by AAO-HNS class A to B and 58% by word recognition class 1 to 2 in the very same patients, with "a different ruler = 24 percentage points" written between the two bars and all four labels attached to each. The second panel shows the probability bands from the 2018 Congress of Neurological Surgeons hearing preservation guideline, the one document that puts all three roads in a single table on one definition of serviceable hearing (AAO-HNS class A or B, or Gardner-Robertson class 1 to 2) and one set of time points: radiosurgery 50% to 75% at two years, 50% to 75% at five and 25% to 50% at ten; microsurgery for small to medium sporadic tumours 25% to 50% in all three cells; conservative observation 75% to 100%, 50% to 75% and 25% to 50%. The panel also records that for patients with baseline class A on observation the guideline writes that the ten-year cell has insufficient data to judge; that no pooled number of patients is given because these are bands synthesised from a systematic review rather than a single study; that every recommendation is Level 3 evidence whose verb is "should be counselled that there is a probability of", making them bands for explaining rather than for ranking; and that the only prognostic factor shared by all three roads is that better word recognition and pure-tone threshold before treatment, and a smaller tumour, raise the chance of preservation. The third panel draws the V-REX randomised trial: single-centre, observer-blinded, 100 patients, four years, with tumour volume ratio as the primary endpoint - 0.87 of baseline in the radiosurgery arm (95% confidence interval 0.66 to 1.15) against 1.51 in the wait-and-scan arm, ratio 1.73, p=.002. Beside it sit 26 small squares of which only one is lit and 25 are grey, showing that 25 of the 26 prespecified secondary endpoints showed no difference and that hearing and quality of life are among those 25. Below: 21 patients (42%) in the wait-and-scan arm had radiosurgery within four years because of growth and 28 (56%) ended with no treatment, while 45 (94%) in the radiosurgery arm had no further treatment; and surgery versus radiosurgery has never been randomised. The fourth panel is headed "hearing is falling on both roads" and strikes out two sentences with crosses: "radiosurgery preserves hearing better" and "observation preserves hearing better". Four labelled cards follow: observation, 156 patients, nine and a half years - AAO-HNS class A fell from 19% of patients to 3%, word recognition from 60% to 34%, pure tone from 51 to 72 dB; observation, 636 patients, ten years - 53% had word recognition above 70% at diagnosis and 31% still did at ten years, while 88% of those starting at 100% still had good hearing; observation versus radiosurgery, 237 patients, mean 55 months - loss of serviceable hearing 54/71 (76%) with observation and 34/53 (64%) with radiosurgery, with no statistical difference; and fractionated radiotherapy, 21 patients - 8 (38%) still had serviceable hearing at two years and none at ten years. The last two cards note that the sources write only "serviceable hearing" without stating a grading system. The same panel records what radiosurgery does buy - tumour control and one fewer re-treatment: a systematic review of 24 studies and 4,079 tumours gives 10-year control of 90.93% against 65.24% in 1,959 untreated tumours, an absolute difference of 25.7 percentage points and a number needed to treat of 4, falling to 18.31% and a number needed to treat of 6 in Koos class 1 tumours, while a prospective comparison of 237 patients shows radiosurgery cutting re-treatment to roughly a tenth. The fifth panel draws five measuring sticks of different lengths to show that "tumour control" has no shared definition: a 20% increase in maximum diameter, a 10% increase in volume, a 2 mm increase in maximum diameter, the need for further treatment, and the authors' own definition of "no further treatment", which they acknowledge may underestimate the failure rate. It states that a radiosurgery control rate must not be placed next to a recurrence rate after gross total resection because they are two different rulers, and that whether transient enlargement counts as progression or control depends on each study's threshold and time window; and it gives one fully labelled counter-example - single-session radiosurgery, 1,409 patients, median follow-up six point seven years, pure tone below 50 dB and word recognition above 50%, preservation 59.4%, with the individual ten-year figures scattered between 23% and 58%. The sixth panel sets out the three things worth asking about on the surgical road: the chance of keeping hearing (8 studies, five years or more, AAO-HNS A or B, 310 patients, 60%, in a selected group), the facial nerve (long-term House-Brackmann grade 1 in 228 patients, 94%; persistent facial palsy 3% to 46%; surgical mortality 0.5%; after radiosurgery new facial deficit 1.3% and new trigeminal neuropathy 3.2%) and pain and cerebrospinal fluid leak (2.7% in one surgeon's series of 146 patients). It notes that a meta-analysis of 6,889 patients found no significant difference between three approaches in hearing preservation or facial nerve function, with a non-significant risk ratio for leak, and explains the House-Brackmann scale: grades 1 to 3 the eye still closes on effort, from grade 4 it does not, grade 5 leaves slight movement and grade 6 is complete palsy, with grade 4 as the line that matters. The seventh panel places three citable documents that disagree side by side - the Brazilian Society of Otology guideline favouring surgery for serviceable hearing as a strong recommendation, the Congress of Neurological Surgeons bands pointing the other way, and a systematic review of six retrospective cohorts favouring radiosurgery - under the line "I am not going to pick a side for you"; and below it quality of life, from a meta-analysis of 16 studies and 3,745 patients on the PANQOL scale: observation 69.1 (66.0 to 72.2, n=1,430), radiosurgery 66.9 (62.7 to 71.2, n=864) and microsurgery 61.3 (57.2 to 65.4, n=1,451), with no gap exceeding the minimal clinically important difference and high heterogeneity, plus a prospective comparison of 455 patients followed a mean of four and a half years in which only tinnitus differed, rising 0.8 points with radiosurgery (p=0.005) against a non-significant 0.2 rise with observation and 0.2 fall with surgery. The eighth panel quotes the Taiwanese regulation word for word - "F. A unilateral intracranial cerebellopontine angle acoustic neuroma less than 2.5 cm in width (not including the internal auditory canal)" - and flags beside it that this is a reimbursement threshold and not a treatment threshold, explaining that items 37028B and 37029B are both effective from 1 April 2026, that the indication clause names acoustic neuroma and requires one of six sub-clauses A to F, that 37028B has a general threshold of a diameter under three centimetres or a volume of fifteen cubic centimetres or less while 37029B allows three-dimensional diameters no greater than 3.5 by 3.5 by 3.5 centimetres or a volume of twenty cubic centimetres, that both limit the number of lesions to three, and that every case must be applied for in advance. The figure closes with four questions to take to the clinic: which management are you assessing for my size, location and audiogram; which grading system, how many years, how many patients and which treatment lie behind the preservation rate you quote; if I observe, how often is the scan and what would change the decision; and if I have surgery, what are your own unit's facial nerve and leak figures.

級以上、會侵犯的大腺瘤與巨大腺瘤，共識寫的才是泌乳素瘤以藥物為先；生長激素瘤分泌生長激素，第一線是手術；庫欣病分泌促腎上腺皮質素，第一線是手術；非功能性不分泌，還沒壓到視路的先追蹤，已經有視野缺損、眼肌麻痺，或腫瘤貼著、壓著視神經與視交叉的轉手術。同格註明分泌促甲狀腺素的腺瘤確實存在，但少到不在這份排序裡，可引用的比例沒有查到。第三格是各型佔多少，三組族群三個答案，各自標來源與人數：比利時列日省橫斷面密集找案，71,972 裂隙囊腫為主。第四格畫一公分那條線：小於一公分叫微偶然瘤、一公分以上叫大偶然瘤，這是約定俗成的分界，不是生物學上的斷點；列日那個世代裡診斷當下已經是大腺瘤的佔 42.6%；這條線不決定第一線治療，它決定的是壓到誰——往上頂到視交叉就是視野缺損，往兩側長進海綿竇就是複視或眼皮下垂。同格另畫英國 Banbury 63 人從症狀出現到被診斷的中位數：泌乳素瘤一年半、非功能性 0.8 年、肢端肥大症 4.5 年、促腎上腺皮質素腺瘤 7 年，並註明帶著「已經找了很久」走進門診的人多半是後面那兩型。第五格是高泌乳素血症的鑑別：要先排懷孕，然後是藥物（完整藥名清單沒有取得所以不列，請把所有在吃的藥整單帶去）、甲狀腺功能低下、巨泌乳素（泌乳素和免疫球蛋白結合成的大分子，驗得到卻沒有生物活性，臨床表現和數值對不起來的人要篩檢）、柄部壓迫效應（輕度到中度升高時原因可能是它壓住了垂體柄，這種情況吃藥腫瘤不會縮、而且還是可能繼續長，所以影像要照常追）。同格把 hook effect 畫成兩根長條：真正的泌乳素很高，驗出來的數值卻只有正常或輕微升高；說明機轉是泌乳素高到把檢驗試劑的捕捉抗體佔滿，反而驗出一個假的低值，要把血清稀釋後重測；並寫出另一半——這件事在新一代的化學冷光免疫分析已經不常見，要不要稀釋重驗是醫師的判斷。第六格是非功能性的追蹤時程，來自 2011 年那份偶然瘤指引：影像方面，大偶然瘤第一次掃描後六個月再照一次 MRI、微偶然瘤一年後再照，接下來三年大的每年一次、微的每一到兩年一次，之後逐漸拉長；抽血方面，大偶然瘤初次檢查後六個月再評估一次垂體功能低下、之後每年一次，臨床表現、病史與 MRI 都沒有變化的微偶然瘤，指引逐字寫的是不需要再驗垂體功能低下。自然史是未治療的非分泌腺瘤最多有 25% 在觀察期間會長大，每年 0.4 到 1.0 公釐，這是最大徑的量法，換成體積量法會得到不一樣的答案。第七格是另一個方向：列日世代裡診斷當下就有 20.6% 的人有垂體功能低下（n=68）；偶然瘤指引對所有偶然瘤病人的建議都是荷爾蒙過多和荷爾蒙不足兩個方向同時評估；可以逐字引的抽血清單來自英國內分泌學會的急診指引——cortisol、TSH、free T4、prolactin、IGF-1、LH、FSH，男性加 testosterone、女性加 en_alt: Schematic showing how pituitary adenomas are triaged by what they secrete, and what the first line of treatment is for each type. It opens with the foundation of the whole triage: the incidentaloma guideline lists the conditions that should be referred for surgery and its last item reads, word for word, "Hypersecreting tumors other than prolactinomas" - secreting tumours go to surgery as a rule, and the prolactinoma is singled out as the exception; a crossed circle beside it marks that this must not be read as "pituitary tumours are all treated with drugs first". Four types then sit side by side. The prolactinoma secretes prolactin and its first line is medical treatment, but the same cell records that the 2025 prolactinoma consensus (a Chinese one, not the Pituitary Society) draws the line on the shape of the tumour: for Knosp grade 0 to 1, well-circumscribed microadenomas and macroadenomas, surgery is also one of the first-line options, and only at Knosp grade 2 or above, and for invasive macroadenomas and giant adenomas, does the consensus write that a dopamine agonist is the first choice. The somatotroph adenoma secretes growth hormone and its first line is surgery. Cushing's disease secretes adrenocorticotrophic hormone and its first line is surgery. The non-functioning adenoma secretes nothing and is followed up while the visual pathway is clear, with referral for surgery if there is already a visual field defect or ophthalmoplegia or if the tumour abuts or compresses the optic nerve and chiasm. A note records that thyrotrophin-secreting adenomas exist but are too rare to appear in the ranking and that no citable proportion was found. The third panel gives how common each type is, in three cohorts with three answers, each labelled with its source and number: cross-sectional intensive case-finding in the province of Liege, Belgium, found 68 clinically relevant pituitary adenomas among 71,972 people, a prevalence of 94 per 100,000 (95% confidence interval 72.2 to 115.8), split as prolactinoma 66%, non-secreting 14.7%, somatotroph adenoma 13.2% and Cushing's disease 5.9%; the community-based study in Banbury in the United Kingdom found 63 cases among 81,149 people, split 57%, 28%, 11% and 2%; and a workshop hosted by the Pituitary Society assembled ranges of prolactinoma 50 to 60%, non-functioning 20 to 40%, somatotroph adenoma 10 to 15% and corticotroph adenoma 5 to 8%. The panel explains that they do not line up because who was scanned, how cases were found and how the denominator was counted all differ, and adds that something in the sellar region is not necessarily an adenoma: in a surgical series of sellar masses 91% were pituitary adenomas and about 9% were not of pituitary origin, that tenth being mostly craniopharyngiomas and Rathke cleft cysts. The fourth panel draws the one-centimetre line: under one centimetre is a microincidentaloma, one centimetre or more a macroincidentaloma, a conventional boundary and not a biological breakpoint; 42.6% of the Liege cohort were already macroadenomas at diagnosis; and the line does not decide the first line of treatment but decides who is being pressed on - upwards into the optic chiasm means a visual field defect, sideways into the cavernous sinus means double vision or a drooping eyelid. The same panel shows the median time from symptom onset to diagnosis in the 63 Banbury patients: one and a half years for prolactinoma, 0.8 years for non-functioning adenoma, 4.5 years for acromegaly and 7 years for corticotroph adenoma, noting that people who arrive having been searching a long time are usually one of the last two types. The fifth panel is the differential for a high prolactin: pregnancy has to be excluded first, then medicines (no citable complete list of drug names was obtained so none is given; bring the whole list of what you take), thyroid function, macroprolactin (prolactin bound to immunoglobulin, detectable but without biological activity, to be screened for when the clinical picture and the value do not match) and the stalk compression effect (when the rise is only mild to moderate the cause may be pressure on the pituitary stalk, in which case a drug will not shrink the tumour and it may still grow, so imaging carries on as usual). The hook effect is drawn as two bars: the true prolactin is very high while the assay reports only a normal or mildly raised value, because prolactin saturates the capture antibody of the assay and a false low value is reported, so the serum should be diluted and re-measured; the other half is written too - this has become uncommon with newer chemiluminescent immunoassays, and whether to dilute and re-test is a clinical judgement. The sixth panel is the follow-up schedule for the non-functioning road from the 2011 incidentaloma guideline: on imaging, a macroincidentaloma is rescanned by MRI six months after the first scan and a microincidentaloma at one year, then for the next three years yearly for macro and every one to two years for micro, lengthening gradually thereafter; on blood tests, a macroincidentaloma is reassessed for hypopituitarism six months after the initial work-up and then yearly, while for a microincidentaloma with no change in clinical picture, history or MRI the guideline writes word for word that repeat testing for hypopituitarism is not needed. The natural history is that up to 25% of untreated non-secreting adenomas enlarge during observation, mostly slowly at 0.4 to 1.0 mm a year, on a maximum-diameter measurement that would give a different answer by volume. The seventh panel covers the other direction: 20.6% of the Liege cohort already had hypopituitarism at diagnosis (n=68); the guideline recommends assessing both too much and too little hormone at once; and the quotable list of tests comes from the emergency guidance of the Society for Endocrinology - cortisol, TSH, free T4, prolactin, IGF-1, LH, FSH, plus testosterone in men and oestradiol in women - which is the emergency setting, with clinic testing left to the doctor. The eighth panel gives the Taiwanese clauses: pasireotide is restricted to patients with Cushing's disease for whom pituitary surgery is not possible or has failed, and octreotide and lanreotide to patients with acromegaly inadequately controlled by surgery, radiotherapy or dopamine agonist therapy - by placing the drug after surgery the clause concedes that surgery is the step taken first; the tests are listed in the fee schedule as prolactin 09120C at 150 points, IGF-1 24023B at 480 points, cortisol 09113C at 240 points and ACTH 09119B at 450 points, along with the stimulation tests for each axis, although being listed does not mean a claim will be approved. The figure closes with four questions in order: which hormones were tested and where did each result fall; is this a microadenoma or a macroadenoma and is it touching the optic chiasm; if the prolactin is high, have medicines, thyroid function and stalk compression been excluded; and is my pituitary function sufficient and does anything need replacing.

zh_alt: 示意圖：腦下垂體腺瘤病人的兩個急症，畫成上下兩條分開的時間軸，另外在最底下畫第三條與它們無關的術後時間軸。圖的開頭先聲明：這張圖不寫劑量，也不寫任何自行調整類固醇的方法——壓力情境下類固醇該怎麼處理是有標準答案的臨床問題，而那個答案要由你的內分泌科醫師針對你本人寫在紙上，包含吃多少、吃到什麼時候。第一條軸是垂體中風。起點是突然的劇烈頭痛，圖上註明急性劇烈頭痛是最常見也最早出現的表現；英國內分泌學會 2016 年的內分泌急症指引把觸發條件寫成：任何人出現急性劇烈頭痛，再加上下列任一項，就要把垂體中風列入考慮——已排除蛛網膜下腔出血與腦膜炎者、有神經眼科徵象者、已知有垂體腫瘤者。從起點分出四條分支：眼肌麻痺，來自海綿竇受影響，最常見的是第三對顱神經麻痺，表現是眼皮下垂、複視、瞳孔變化；視力下降與視野缺損，來自視交叉被壓，最常見的是雙顳側偏盲，也就是兩側外側視野像被遮住；發燒、頸部僵硬、畏光或意識程度下降，看起來很像蛛網膜下腔出血或腦膜炎；以及噁心嘔吐，常與頭痛同時出現。四條分支收束到同一個動作格：認出這組組合之後，動作只有一個——當天就到急診，不要等門診、不要自己開車，請家人送或叫救護車；到了檢傷檯，把「我有垂體瘤」或「懷疑垂體中風」這幾個字講出來，因為指引把「已知有垂體腫瘤」列為觸發條件之一。同一條軸旁邊列出誘因清單：高血壓、大手術、垂體的動態刺激試驗、抗凝血劑、凝血功能異常、懷孕、頭部外傷；並列三個事實：這些人裡大約八成事前根本不知道自己的垂體有問題，而症狀又很像其他更常見的神經科疾病；影像上 MRI 是首選，指引寫它在超過九成的病人身上確認了診斷，MRI 不能做時才用電腦斷層；英國 Banbury 的社區研究裡 63 位垂體腺瘤病人有 5 位（7.9%）是以典型的垂體中風被發現，那是「以中風表現被診斷」的比例，不是「有垂體瘤的人日後會中風」的比例，分母不一樣。這條軸的最後是到了急診的處置順序：先穩住；血行動力學不穩、意識改變或視力視野嚴重受損者，給經驗性的類固醇（指引的用字是「可能救命」）；緊急轉神經外科與內分泌的聯合團隊。第二條軸是腎上腺功能不足，慢得多也更容易被錯過：累、沒力氣、站起來頭暈，拖到某天發燒生病才整個垮下來。症狀分成五格：全身——疲倦、沒有力氣、體重下降；血壓——血壓低、姿勢性頭暈與低血壓、昏倒、嚴重時低血容性休克；肚子——腹痛、按壓會痛、噁心嘔吐；發燒與意識——發燒、意識混亂、嗜睡、嚴重時譫妄或昏迷；背部與腿部——抽筋或痙攣，指引特別註明這一項很容易被當成別的問題追著跑。另有一格畫皮膚：垂體來源（次發性）的皮膚是蒼白的，指引形容那是像雪花石膏一樣的膚色，這一格打勾；皮膚變黑是原發性腎上腺功能不足的特徵，不是垂體來源的，這一格打叉。同格寫著：一半以上的腎上腺功能不足，是在急性危象發生之後才被診斷出來的，所以如果你有垂體瘤，「我的腎上腺這一軸夠不夠用」是要主動問的問題，不是等症狀來。另有一條紅字：已經在補充類固醇的人，如果一直吐或一直拉到藥吞不下去，或是出現意識不清、站都站不起來，那就是急診等級的狀況，當天就到急診，並且把你的用藥清單一起帶著。壓力情境被畫成四個要在還沒生病的時候就問清楚的問題：生病、發燒到需要臥床或要吃抗生素的時候，我的類固醇要怎麼處理，請寫在紙上給我；一直吐或一直拉、藥根本吞不下去的時候呢，那時候該怎麼辦、要打給誰；要開刀、要全身麻醉、或要做大腸鏡前的清腸，我該先告訴誰、提前多久講；我需不需要家裡備一支可以注射的，誰來教我和家人怎麼打、多久檢查一次有沒有過期。同格說明這四個問題對應的是指引明文列為醫師責任的幾件事：教育病人與家屬、教會自我注射並備好緊急注射的藥、定期複查、給一組緊急聯絡電話；並補上兩樣硬體——類固醇急救卡與醫療警示手環，卡片要隨身帶、遇到任何醫療人員就拿出來，官方頁面說明它的功能是提醒接手的醫護，給十六歲以上的成人用；台灣有沒有對應的官方卡片制度，查不到可以引用的說明。圖的最下方用一條明顯的分隔線隔出第三件事，並標明「下面這一條是另一件事」：手術之後的那條時間軸，不要跟上面兩個急症混著記。尿崩——881 位經蝶竇手術的資料裡，術前沒有尿崩的 857 人術後立即出現尿崩 18.3%，需要長期用藥的永久性尿崩只有 2%；低血鈉——低血鈉是出院之後的事，一個 300 人的隨機試驗裡，自由飲水組整體低血鈉 31.9%、再住院 6.4%。圖的結尾是一張折起來放進錢包的紙：寫上診斷、目前在吃的荷爾蒙補充藥、你的內分泌科醫師與聯絡電話，還有上面那四個問題的答案，折起來放進錢包，再拍一張傳給家人；下一次門診把它拿出來讓醫師補幾個字。它要擋的不是腫瘤，是「等到垮下來才被診斷」這個順序。
en_alt: Schematic of the two emergencies that can face someone with a pituitary adenoma, drawn as two separate timelines with a third, unrelated postoperative timeline set apart at the bottom. It opens with a statement: this figure carries no doses and no method for adjusting steroids yourself, because how steroids are handled under stress is a clinical question with a standard answer that, including how much and for how long, has to be written down on paper for the patient personally by their endocrinologist. The first axis is pituitary apoplexy. It starts from a sudden severe headache, noted as the commonest and earliest manifestation, with the trigger from the 2016 Society for Endocrinology endocrine emergency guidance: consider pituitary apoplexy in anyone with an acute severe headache plus any one of the following - those in whom subarachnoid haemorrhage and meningitis have been excluded, those with neuro-ophthalmic signs, and those with a known pituitary tumour. Four branches come off that start point: ophthalmoplegia from involvement of the cavernous sinus, most commonly a third nerve palsy with a drooping eyelid, double vision and pupil changes; reduced visual acuity and visual field defects from compression of the optic chiasm, most commonly a bitemporal hemianopia in which the outer field of each eye seems covered over; fever, neck stiffness, photophobia or reduced consciousness, which can look very like subarachnoid haemorrhage or meningitis; and nausea and vomiting alongside the headache. The four branches converge on a single action: go to the emergency department the same day, without waiting for a clinic appointment and without driving yourself, having a relative take you or calling an ambulance, and at triage saying the words "I have a pituitary tumour" or "possible pituitary apoplexy", because the guidance lists a known pituitary tumour as one of the triggers. Beside the axis is the list of precipitants - hypertension, major surgery, dynamic testing of the pituitary gland, anticoagulation, coagulopathy, pregnancy and head trauma - and three facts: about four in five of these people had no idea anything was wrong with their pituitary beforehand and the symptoms resemble commoner neurological conditions; MRI is the imaging of choice and the guidance states it confirmed the diagnosis in more than nine in ten patients, with CT used only when MRI cannot be done; and in the Banbury community study 5 of 63 patients with a pituitary adenoma (7.9%) were found through a typical pituitary apoplexy, which is the proportion diagnosed by presenting with apoplexy and not the proportion of people with a pituitary tumour who will later have one, the denominators being different. The axis ends with the order of management in the emergency department: stabilise first; empirical steroid replacement for those who are haemodynamically unstable, whose consciousness is altered or whose visual acuity or fields are severely affected, which the guidance calls potentially lifesaving; and urgent referral to a joint neurosurgical and endocrine team. The second axis is adrenal insufficiency, far slower and far easier to miss - tired, no strength, dizzy on standing, until a febrile illness one day brings the whole thing down. Its symptoms are grouped in five cells: whole body - fatigue, lack of energy, weight loss; blood pressure - low blood pressure, postural dizziness and hypotension, collapse, hypovolaemic shock in severe cases; abdomen - abdominal pain, tenderness on pressing, nausea and vomiting; fever and consciousness - fever, confusion, somnolence, delirium or coma in severe cases; and back and legs - cramps or spasms, with the guidance noting specifically that this one is easily chased as some other problem. A further cell covers the skin: pituitary in origin, that is secondary, is ticked and the skin is pale, described in the guidance as an alabaster-like complexion; darkening of the skin is crossed out as belonging to primary adrenal insufficiency and not to the pituitary kind. The same cell records that in more than half of people with adrenal insufficiency the diagnosis is only made after an acute crisis, so for anyone with a pituitary tumour "is this axis doing enough" is a question to ask actively rather than to wait for symptoms to answer. A red line adds that anyone already on steroid replacement who is vomiting or has diarrhoea to the point where tablets will not stay down, or who becomes confused or cannot stand, is in an emergency and should go to the emergency department the same day with their medication list, rather than sitting it out at home. Stress situations are drawn as four questions to have answered before becoming ill: when I am ill or febrile enough to need bed rest or antibiotics, what should happen to my steroid, please write it down for me; and when I am vomiting or have diarrhoea and cannot keep the tablets down, what then and who do I call; before an operation, a general anaesthetic or bowel preparation for a colonoscopy, who should I tell and how far ahead; and do I need an injection kept at home, who will teach me and my family to use it and how often should we check it has not expired. The panel explains that these four match what the guidance lists as the clinician's responsibilities - educating patient and family, teaching self-injection and supplying the emergency injection, regular review and a set of emergency phone numbers - and adds two pieces of hardware, a steroid emergency card and a medical alert bracelet, the card to be carried at all times and shown to any healthcare professional, its official function being to prompt the staff taking over and its use being for adults aged sixteen and over, with no citable statement found on whether Taiwan has an equivalent scheme. At the foot of the figure a clear divider sets apart a third thing, labelled "what follows is a different thing": the timeline after surgery, not to be remembered alongside the two emergencies above. Diabetes insipidus - in a series of 881 transsphenoidal operations, among the 857 without it beforehand, 18.3% had it immediately after surgery, while permanent diabetes insipidus needing long-term treatment was only 2%. Hyponatraemia - something that happens after discharge, with 31.9% overall and 6.4% readmission in the free-fluid group of a randomised trial of 300 patients. The figure closes with a piece of paper folded into a wallet: the diagnosis, the hormone replacement being taken, the endocrinologist and their phone number, and the answers to those four questions, folded into the wallet and photographed for the family, to be handed over at the next clinic visit for a few words to be added - what it is there to stop being not the tumour but the sequence in which the diagnosis only arrives after the collapse.

zh_alt: 示意圖：NF2 相關神經鞘瘤病怎麼用同一個基因同時解釋多發腦膜瘤與雙側前庭神經鞘瘤。圖的開頭是命名那一格，標題是「不是改名，是這個詞被退掉了」，逐字引 2022 年國際共識：「在修訂後的命名中，neurofibromatosis 2 這個詞已經被退場，以改善診斷的特異性。」新名稱是 NF2-related schwannomatosis，中文可叫 NF2 相關神經鞘瘤病，縮寫 NF2-SWN；理由是強調這群疾病在表現上的重疊、減少跟第 1 型神經纖維瘤病的誤診；新準則也把鑲嵌型直接寫進條文；拿著寫「NF2」的舊報告查資料會查到兩套詞彙，它們指同一件事，但內容不完全一樣。圖的中心是一個節點：NF2（第 22 號染色體）。節點上寫三件事：NF2-SWN 是體染色體顯性的腫瘤易感症候群，帶因者容易長出神經鞘瘤、腦膜瘤與室管膜瘤；NF2 也是偶發型腦膜瘤最常見的驅動突變，Alliance A071401 之所以只收帶體細胞 NF2 突變的腦膜瘤，設計理由逐字就是「腦膜瘤中 NF2 突變的優勢地位」；一個人同時長兩種瘤，是同一條路壞掉的兩個出口。從中心節點往左右各分出一條：左分支是多發腦膜瘤——一生當中最多八成的 NF2-SWN 病人會長腦膜瘤（15 篇、937 位病人、3,637 顆的統合分析）；監測中的 2,082 顆腫瘤加權平均生長速率每年 0.508 立方公分；監測期間長出新生腦膜瘤的病人比例 24.6%，但 95% 信賴區間非常寬（2.73 到 58.7），只有三篇研究有資料；被手術切除的只有 203 顆（彙整復發風險 12.5%），接受立體定位放射手術的 665 顆（惡化風險 6.29%）；國際共識另補約 10% 會長得快（一份研究把快定義為每年 2 立方公分以上），20% 的病人會長出新的腦膜瘤。右分支是雙側前庭神經鞘瘤——它是 NF2-SWN 的單一充分診斷條件；影像該多久做一次要調整，這群人的聽神經瘤生長速率變異較大，可能需要比偶發型更頻繁的影像；雙側的人在對側腫瘤切除後，這側的生長速率可能加快。兩條分支下方註明：注意分母，手術與放射手術加起來的顆數遠少於監測中的顆數，「最多八成會長」不等於「八成的人要治療」。另有一段接到放射線那一面：放射線引起的腦膜瘤裡，NF2 的點突變比偶發型少，但基因融合事件反而較多，推測是放射造成雙股斷裂後修復出錯的結果；同一個基因，被兩種完全不同的機制打壞。接著是診斷準則，符合任一項即可診斷：第一，雙側前庭神經鞘瘤；第二，在至少兩個解剖位置不同的 NF2 相關腫瘤（神經鞘瘤、腦膜瘤或室管膜瘤）裡找到同一個 NF2 致病變異，附註是若血液這類未受影響組織裡的變異等位基因頻率明顯低於 50%，診斷是鑲嵌型；第三，兩個主要條件，或一個主要條件加兩個次要條件——主要條件是單側前庭神經鞘瘤、有一位非手足的一等親罹患 NF2-SWN、兩顆以上的腦膜瘤（單獨一顆只算次要條件）、在未受影響組織中找到 NF2 致病變異；次要條件是室管膜瘤、腦膜瘤、神經鞘瘤，加上幼年型白內障、視網膜錯構瘤、40 歲以下的視網膜前膜。同格另列兩件容易寫錯的事：雙側聽神經瘤沒有年齡上限，2019 年曾有人提議加一個 70 歲的切點，共識決定不加，理由逐字是「避免臨床醫師因此不去檢查年紀較大的病人」；單側聽神經瘤加上兩顆以上其他部位的神經鞘瘤時，確認 NF2-SWN 之前應先排除 LZTR1 的變異。再往下是 bevacizumab 的聽力反應，先給反應定義：三個前瞻試驗的主要終點都是用字詞辨識分數定義的聽力反應——聽懂一組標準字詞的比例改善並維持一段時間，不是主觀覺得比較好聽。三筆數字各帶族群：14 位 NF2 病人、目標耳有進展性聽力喪失、用藥 46 週，確認的聽力反應 5/14，36%（95% 信賴區間 13 到 65%；反應定義是改善維持三個月以上；沒有病人聽力變差）；22 人的高劑量試驗在六個月時是 9/22，41%，作者的結論是高劑量看來不比標準劑量更有效；9 篇、176 人的系統性回顧聽力改善 36%、穩定 46%、惡化 18%，腫瘤部分縮小 40%、穩定 50%、惡化 10%，嚴重不良反應 13%，作者並點出停藥後有病人腫瘤再長。維持治療的 20 人試驗看得到時間這一維，目標耳免於聽力惡化的比例 48 週是 95%、72 週 89%、98 週降到 70%。同格註明這條路只對 NF2 相關的聽神經瘤開著：2020 年歐洲聽神經瘤指引寫的是，除了用在 NF2 的 bevacizumab 之外，藥物治療沒有角色；偶發型的人不要把這些數字套到自己身上。圖的底部是一整欄鑑別：多發腦膜瘤不等於 NF2。列出 SMARCB1（第 22 號染色體相關的 SMARCB1 神經鞘瘤病，也可以有多顆顱內腦膜瘤）、LZTR1（單側聽神經瘤加上其他部位神經鞘瘤時要先排除的那一個）、BAP1 腫瘤易感症候群、SUFU 家族性腦膜瘤易感、SMARCE1 造成的家族性透明細胞腦膜瘤，以及過去的放射線暴露——病史要問清楚過去的放射線暴露，因為腦膜瘤本來就是久遠放射暴露後常見的續發腫瘤，放射線引起的腦膜瘤裡多顆的就佔 17.3%。同格引國際共識：跟偶發型比，NF2-SWN 病人發病年齡較輕、更容易長出多顆腦膜瘤，所以這類表現的人應接受生殖系 NF2 與 SMARCE1 變異的篩檢；要不要做、怎麼做是遺傳諮詢門診的事，不是自己去掛號驗。接著是鑲嵌型那一格：1,055 位沒有上一代家族史的新發個案裡，確診或推定鑲嵌型的有 232 人（22.0%）；因為非鑲嵌型的變異偵測率本身只有 36.7%，作者推算整體的鑲嵌比例可能高達 59.7%；這比例還隨發病年齡大幅變化，20 歲以前以雙側聽神經瘤表現的人是 21.7%，60 歲以上是 80.7%；鑲嵌型的病人本人仍然可能病得很重，需要完整的臨床監測與介入；檢測也不是抽一管血就結束，要驗血液，理想上再驗兩個以上來自神經系統不同區域的相關腫瘤，才分得出是鑲嵌型還是生殖系。這一格用一條紅色的橫幅明寫：家屬的再發風險，這張圖不寫百分比——那要由遺傳諮詢師依你的檢驗結果算。最後是台灣端，分成查得到與查不到兩格：查得到的是健保條文裡有「遺傳諮詢中心」這個角色，25021B「染色體檢查（特殊）」的規範逐字寫著限衛生福利部認證之遺傳諮詢中心申請實施、作為一般性篩檢者非屬給付範圍；查不到的是全表裡沒有任何以 NF2 或神經纖維瘤命名的檢測項目，以及 NF2-SWN 在不在台灣公告的罕見疾病名單裡——《罕見疾病防治及藥物法》第 3 條寫的是由中央主管機關依盛行率基準指定公告，法源查得到、名單取不到，請向遺傳諮詢中心確認。圖的結尾寫：回診前先把家族史寫成一張表，誰有過腦部或脊椎腫瘤、聽力問題、幼年白內障，準則裡好幾條要靠它；到了診間問的是「我這個表現需不需要轉遺傳諮詢」，而不是自己先去驗。
en_alt: Schematic of how NF2-related schwannomatosis explains both multiple meningiomas and bilateral vestibular schwannomas through a single gene. It opens with the naming panel, headed "this is not a rename, the term was retired", quoting the 2022 international consensus word for word: "In the revised nomenclature, the term neurofibromatosis 2 has been retired to improve diagnostic specificity." The new name is NF2-related schwannomatosis, abbreviated NF2-SWN; the reasoning is to emphasise the overlap in how these conditions present and to reduce misdiagnosis as neurofibromatosis type 1; the new criteria also write the mosaic form directly into the text; and searching with an old report that says "NF2" turns up two sets of vocabulary that refer to the same thing without being identical. At the centre of the figure sits one node: NF2, on chromosome 22. Three things are written on it: NF2-SWN is an autosomal dominant tumour predisposition syndrome whose carriers are prone to schwannomas, meningiomas and ependymomas; NF2 is also the commonest driver mutation in sporadic meningioma, which is why Alliance A071401 enrolled only meningiomas with a somatic NF2 mutation, its stated design reason being "the predominance of NF2 mutations in meningiomas"; and someone growing both tumours is showing two exits from the same broken road. Two branches run from that node. The left branch is multiple meningiomas: up to 80% of people with NF2-SWN develop a meningioma over a lifetime, from a meta-analysis of 15 studies, 937 patients and 3,637 tumours; the 2,082 tumours under surveillance grew at a weighted mean of 0.508 cubic centimetres a year; new meningiomas appeared during surveillance in 24.6% of patients, though the 95% confidence interval is very wide at 2.73 to 58.7 and only three studies had data; only 203 tumours were surgically removed, with a pooled recurrence risk of 12.5%, and 665 had stereotactic radiosurgery, with a progression risk of 6.29%; and the international consensus adds that about 10% grow quickly, one study defining quickly as more than 2 cubic centimetres a year, and that 20% of patients grow a new meningioma. The right branch is bilateral vestibular schwannomas: on their own sufficient for the diagnosis of NF2-SWN; imaging intervals have to be adjusted because growth rates vary more in this group than in sporadic tumours and imaging may need to be more frequent; and in someone with bilateral tumours the growth rate on one side may accelerate after the tumour on the other side is removed. Below the branches a note warns to watch the denominators, since surgery and radiosurgery together account for far fewer tumours than surveillance, so "up to 80% will grow one" is not "80% of people need treatment". A further passage connects to the radiation side: in radiation-induced meningiomas, point mutations in NF2 are less common than in sporadic ones while gene fusion events are more common, thought to follow faulty repair of radiation-induced double-strand breaks - the same gene broken by two entirely different mechanisms. The criteria follow, any one of which is enough for the diagnosis: first, bilateral vestibular schwannomas; second, the same pathogenic NF2 variant found in at least two anatomically distinct NF2-related tumours, that is schwannoma, meningioma or ependymoma, with the note that if the variant allele frequency in unaffected tissue such as blood is clearly below 50% the diagnosis is the mosaic form; and third, two major criteria or one major plus two minor criteria, where the major criteria are a unilateral vestibular schwannoma, a first-degree relative other than a sibling with NF2-SWN, two or more meningiomas with a single one counting only as a minor criterion, and a pathogenic NF2 variant in unaffected tissue, while the minor criteria are ependymoma, meningioma, schwannoma, juvenile cataract, retinal hamartoma and epiretinal membrane under the age of 40. Two easily mistaken points are listed alongside: there is no upper age limit on bilateral vestibular schwannomas, a cut-off at 70 having been proposed in 2019 and rejected by the consensus in order to "avoid clinicians not investigating older patients"; and for a unilateral vestibular schwannoma with two or more schwannomas at other sites, an LZTR1 variant should be excluded before NF2-SWN is confirmed. Next comes the hearing response to bevacizumab, preceded by its response definition: in all three prospective trials the primary endpoint was a hearing response defined on word recognition score, an improvement in the proportion of a standard word list understood and maintained for a period of time, and not a subjective sense of hearing better. Three figures follow, each with its population: in 14 patients with NF2 and progressive hearing loss in the target ear treated for 46 weeks, the confirmed hearing response was 5 of 14, or 36%, with a 95% confidence interval of 13 to 65%, the response defined as improvement maintained for three months or more, and no patient having worse hearing; in a high-dose trial of 22 patients at six months it was 9 of 22, or 41%, with the authors concluding that the high dose does not appear more effective than the standard dose; and in a systematic review of 9 studies and 176 patients, hearing improved in 36%, was stable in 46% and worse in 18%, while tumours partially shrank in 40%, were stable in 50% and progressed in 10%, with serious adverse events in 13% and the authors noting that some tumours regrew after treatment stopped. A maintenance trial of 20 patients shows the time dimension, with target ears free of hearing deterioration in 95% at 48 weeks, 89% at 72 weeks and 70% at 98 weeks. The panel notes that this road is open only for NF2-related vestibular schwannomas, the 2020 European guideline putting it briefly that except for bevacizumab in NF2 there is no role for pharmacotherapy, and that people with a sporadic tumour should not apply these figures to themselves. A full band across the foot of the figure carries the differential: multiple meningiomas do not equal NF2. It lists SMARCB1, that is SMARCB1-related schwannomatosis, also on chromosome 22, which can likewise give multiple intracranial meningiomas; LZTR1, the one to exclude when a unilateral vestibular schwannoma comes with schwannomas elsewhere; BAP1 tumour predisposition syndrome where there are no schwannomas; SUFU-related familial meningioma predisposition; SMARCE1, which causes familial clear cell meningioma; and past radiation exposure, the line most often skipped, because meningioma is a common second tumour long after radiation and 17.3% of radiation-induced meningiomas are multiple. The same panel quotes the international consensus: compared with sporadic cases, people with NF2-SWN present younger and are more likely to grow multiple meningiomas, so anyone presenting like this should be screened for germline NF2 and SMARCE1 variants, with whether and how that is done belonging to a genetic counselling clinic rather than to booking a test yourself. The mosaic panel follows: among 1,055 de novo cases with no family history in the previous generation, 232, or 22.0%, were confirmed or presumed mosaic; because the detection rate for non-mosaic variants is itself only 36.7%, the authors estimate the overall mosaic proportion may be as high as 59.7%; the proportion varies sharply with age at presentation, 21.7% among those presenting with bilateral vestibular schwannomas under 20 and 80.7% among those aged 60 and over; someone with the mosaic form can still be severely affected and needs full clinical surveillance and intervention; and testing is not one tube of blood, since blood is tested and ideally two or more related tumours from different regions of the nervous system as well, to tell the mosaic form from a germline variant. A red band across that panel states plainly that the figure gives no percentage for a relative's risk, because that has to be worked out by a genetic counsellor from the patient's own test results. The Taiwanese section closes the figure in two cells. Found: the reimbursement text does carry the role of a genetic counselling centre, the rules for 25021B, chromosome study (special), stating word for word that it is restricted to genetic counselling centres accredited by the Ministry of Health and Welfare and that use as a general screening test is outside reimbursement. Not found: there is no test item anywhere in the schedule named for NF2 or neurofibromatosis, and whether NF2-SWN appears on the published Taiwanese rare disease list cannot be retrieved, since Article 3 of the Rare Disease Control and Orphan Drug Act says the central competent authority designates and publishes it on a prevalence basis - the legal basis is findable but the list is not, so a genetic counselling centre has to be asked. The figure ends by advising that the family history be written out as a table before the appointment - who has had a brain or spinal tumour, hearing problems, a juvenile cataract, because several of the criteria depend on it - and that the question in the room is whether this presentation needs a genetic counselling referral, rather than booking a test first.
